# Three Friends from Symbiosis Build Beyond Snack, Banana Chips Brand Posts Rs 53 Crore Revenue in FY25 as Losses Widen

Beyond Snack crossed Rs 50 crore revenue in FY25, reporting Rs 53 crore, while losses widened 3.3X to Rs 20.9 crore due to rising overall expenses.

![ ](https://img-cdn.publive.online/fit-in/100x0/filters:format(webp)/startuppedia/media/member_avatars/2026/05/11/2026-05-11t151814780z-whatsapp-image-2026-05-11-at-204741-2026-05-11-20-48-15.jpeg )

Manas Madhu, Jyoti Rajguru, and Gautam Raghuraman - Founders of Beyond Snack

Banana chips brand Beyond Snack reported a 55% surge in revenue to Rs 53 crore in FY25, up from Rs 34.2 crore in FY24, according to its financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Revenue from product sales stood at Rs 52 crore in FY25, compared to Rs 33.7 crore in FY24. The company also recorded Rs 1 crore in other income, primarily from interest on fixed deposits in FY25, up from Rs 50 lakh in FY24.

On the expenditure side, total expenses rose sharply by 82% to Rs 73.8 crore in FY25, from Rs 40.5 crore in FY24. The largest cost component, cost of goods sold, increased by 58% to Rs 32.9 crore in FY25, compared to Rs 20.9 crore in FY24.

Employee benefit expenses nearly doubled to Rs 9.6 crore from Rs 5 crore in FY24. Finance costs and depreciation remained relatively modest at Rs 50 lakh and Rs 1.1 crore, respectively, in FY25. Advertising expenses witnessed a significant 2.3X jump to Rs 8.3 crore in FY25, up from Rs 3.7 crore in FY24.

![TBI Logo](https://static-cdn.publive.online/english-betterindia/media/media_files/2025/10/06/gda-logo-light-2-2025-10-06-15-39-59.png)

The company reported a net loss of Rs 20.9 crore in FY25, marking a 3.3X increase from Rs 6.3 crore in FY24. On a unit economics basis, Beyond Snack spent Rs 1.42 to earn every rupee of revenue in FY25, compared to Rs 1.20 in FY24.

## About Beyond Snack

Beyond Snack is an Indian snacking company specializing in premium, Kerala-style banana chips. Founded in 2020 and headquartered in Alappuzha, Kerala, the brand gained nationwide recognition after its appearance on Shark Tank India Season 1, where it secured investment from Ashneer Grover and Aman Gupta.

The company was founded by Manas Madhu, Jyoti Rajguru, and Gautam Raghuraman, who met while pursuing their MBA at the Symbiosis Institute of Business Management (SIBM), Pune. Beyond Snack uses a fully automated, hands-free production process to ensure hygiene and consistent quality. It recently inaugurated a 60,000 sq ft manufacturing facility in Tumkur, Karnataka.

Its chips are made from Nendran bananas, often referred to as the “King of Bananas.” The brand’s core flavors include Original Salted, Peri Peri, Sour Cream Onion & Parsley, and Salt & Black Pepper.

Beyond Snack products are available through its official website and major e-commerce platforms. The company has also expanded its global presence and is currently available in 12 countries, with plans to enter additional international markets.

The startup raised $8.3 million (Rs 71.84 crore) in a Series A funding round led by 12 Flags Group in January 2025. Earlier, it secured $3.5 million (Rs 29 crore) in a pre-Series A round from NABVENTURES Fund in July 2023.

results.content:
On the expenditure front, advertising and promotional costs declined 17.6 percent to Rs 61 crore in FY26 from Rs 74 crore in FY25. The reduction in marketing expenditure helped lower the company's overall costs despite increases in certain operating expenses.

The cost of materials consumed rose 15.4 percent to Rs 42 crore, broadly in line with the growth in product sales. Employee benefit expenses declined 5.3 percent to Rs 23.6 crore from Rs 24.9 crore in the previous year.

Transportation expenses increased 30 percent to Rs 13 crore, while legal and professional charges fell 36.5 percent to Rs 7.2 crore. Miscellaneous expenses rose 14.8 percent to Rs 22.2 crore from Rs 19 crore in FY25. [...] Commissions paid to sole selling agents also increased significantly, reaching Rs 92 crore during FY26 compared with Rs 15 crore a year earlier. Meanwhile, the cost of materials consumed rose to Rs 162 crore from Rs 79 crore, reflecting the expansion in business activity. Employee benefit expenses more than doubled to Rs 39 crore from Rs 19 crore.

As a result, Innovist's total expenses increased to Rs 662 crore in FY26 from Rs 250 crore in FY25. Despite the higher expenditure, the company reported a profit before tax of Rs 30.5 crore, compared with a loss before tax of Rs 55 lakh in the previous fiscal year. [...] Product sales remained the principal contributor to its operating revenue, generating Rs 676.3 crore in FY26 against Rs 239.1 crore in the previous financial year. Other operating revenue, which includes income from shipping and scrap sales, stood at Rs 9.4 crore during FY26.

The company's revenue growth was accompanied by a substantial increase in spending on customer acquisition and distribution. Advertising and promotional expenses rose more than threefold to Rs 262 crore in FY26 from Rs 84.2 crore in FY25. These expenses accounted for approximately 40 percent of the company's total costs.

{Funding Alert} Beyond Snack Secures $8.3 Mn in Series A Funding to Drive Expansion and Innovation

![Indian Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/art-logo.webp)

BY - [Indian Retailer Bureau](/author/indian-retailer-bureau)  
  Sub Editor  Jan 09, 2025 Jan 09, 2025 / ![IndianRetailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/brandlicense/themes/custom/menshealth/images/vicon.webp)
/ 6 MIN READ

[Follow Us ![Indian Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/follow.webp)](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAiEJjETmBVGGR4AF2qcS42jEMqFAgKIhCYxE5gVRhkeABdqnEuNoxD?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN%3Aen)

![{Funding Alert} Beyond Snack Secures $8.3 Mn in Series A Funding to Drive Expansion and Innovation](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2025-01/Untitled%20design%20-%202025-01-09T122521.923.jpg "{Funding Alert} Beyond Snack Secures $8.3 Mn in Series A Funding to Drive Expansion and Innovation")

Beyond Snack, India’s leading banana chips brand, has raised $8.3 million in a Series A funding round led by 12 Flags Group, a consumer business-focused fund established by Rakesh Kapoor, former global CEO of Reckitt Benckiser. **Existing investor NAB Ventures also participated, increasing its stake in the company, alongside Japanese VC firm Enrission India Capital and other existing investors such as Faad Network. The fresh funds will help Beyond Snack expand into new markets, foster product innovation, and strengthen its supply chain infrastructure.**

> “*Banana chips have often been underrated due to lack of innovation and right technology, but in reality , they are one of the most delightful snacks out there. Hence we decided to drive that innovation and bring the latest technology in banana chips. Our banana chips redefine the snacking experience—delicately thin, irresistibly crispy, and bursting with bold, mouthwatering flavors. They’re more than just a snack; they’re a treat for the senses. This new investment empowers us to bring the unique taste of Beyond Snack banana chips to even more snack enthusiasts across the country, elevating their snacking moments to a whole new level,*” **shared Manas Madhu, Founder, Beyond Snack.**

**Having previously raised $4 million from NAB Ventures, 100X VC, Faad Network, and notable angel investors, Beyond Snack is now a leading banana chips brand across prominent e-commerce and quick commerce platforms, with a retail presence in 20,000 outlets.**

> "*I have never really liked traditional banana chips. They are normally thick, and oily and get stuck in the teeth. But then I tried Beyond Snack, and I was gobsmacked by how delicious, crispy, and uniquely flavored they were. They have captured my taste buds, and as it turns out, also the taste buds of millions across India. We are incredibly excited about the opportunity to partner with the Beyond Snack team. Our investment in Beyond Snack is not just about value creation and growth. It’s also about celebrating and promoting one of India's homegrown brands. We look forward to seeing how this collaboration will drive innovation, and sustainability, and bring joy to snack lovers everywhere*,” **stated Rakesh Kapoor, Founder, 12 Flags Group.**
>
> **Ashish Choudhury, CIO - NABVENTURES LTD commented,** “*We’re excited to deepen our partnership with Beyond Snack. This Follow-on investment underscores NABVENTURES' confidence in Beyond Snack's exceptional performance and its innovative approach to the industry. Beyond Snack is currently deepening backend integration and streamlining its supply chain, further enhancing its efficiency and sustainability within the Agri value chain. This strategic move aligns perfectly with NABVENTURES' vision of driving innovation and fostering a robust and sustainable Agri & Food system.*”
>
> “*We’re thrilled to support Beyond Snack on their journey and look forward to seeing their crispy creations win over taste buds everywhere*,” **said Yusuke Kakimoto, CEO, Enrission India Capital.**

**Founded by Manas Madhu, Jyoti Rajguru, and Gautam Raghuraman, Beyond Snack has been committed to revolutionizing the banana chip market by maintaining the highest hygiene standards through advanced food processing technology.** The company uses superior raw materials, producing its chips from the finest quality bananas and ensuring they are free from artificial colors and synthetic flavors. The brand’s product range includes flavors such as Peri Peri, Salt and Black Pepper, Sour Cream & Onion, and Parsley, in addition to its classic salted variety. Recently, Beyond Snack also launched a Kerala banana chip variant cooked in coconut oil.

**Beyond Snack’s success is not limited to the domestic market. The brand has rapidly expanded its presence to 12 countries and is exploring new international markets, where demand for its products continues to grow.** The company aims to tap further into global markets to drive international expansion.

New Zealand's Only Good Enters India's Beauty and Personal Care Market

![Indian Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/art-logo.webp)

BY - [Indian Retailer Bureau](/author/indian-retailer-bureau)  
 Sub Editor  / 1 MIN READ

[Follow Us ![Indina Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/follow.webp)](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAiEJjETmBVGGR4AF2qcS42jEMqFAgKIhCYxE5gVRhkeABdqnEuNoxD?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN%3Aen)

![New Zealand's Only Good Enters India's Beauty and Personal Care Market](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20Design%20-%202026-10-31T112414.506.jpg)

Only Good, a New Zealand-based beauty and personal care brand owned by Apex Brands, has entered the Indian market through Kiwiyāna, the authorised distributor of Apex Brands in India. **The brand's initial India portfolio comprises seven hand and body washes certified natural by Biorius.**

The India entry marks the brand's expansion into the country's personal care market, where it aims to introduce New Zealand-made beauty and personal care products to Indian consumers. **In its home market, Only Good also offers refills and baby care products as part of its broader portfolio.**

**The entry comes against the backdrop of increasing trade relations between India and New Zealand, with personal care emerging as another category for cross-border business opportunities.**

> “With the India-New Zealand free trade agreement now in force, I am glad to see New Zealand brands reaching Indian homes across more categories, including personal care. Trade between our two countries has already doubled since 2023, and expanding into consumer goods is a natural next step as commercial momentum builds,” **said Graham Rouse, Trade Commissioner / Consul General - India & South Asia, New Zealand Trade & Enterprise.**

**Only Good's hand and body wash collection is available in four variants: Coconut Milk, Sage & Lime Zest, Peach & Honeysuckle, and Cedarwood & Juniper.** The formulations incorporate ingredients such as prickly pear, jojoba seed oil, aloe vera, sage, pomegranate, lime pearl, and Vinanza Kiwi, an extract obtained from kiwifruit skins grown in New Zealand.

> **Akash Sood, Co-founder & Director, Kiwiyāna said,** "People put real thought into their bathrooms, but the bottle beside the shower or sink is often an afterthought. Only Good's bottle is designed to be kept out on the counter, and kept for years."

**The products are packaged in bottles made from recycled and sugarcane-based HDPE. Instead of conventional plastic labels, the brand uses artwork screen-printed directly onto the bottles.** The packaging has received the WorldStar 2025 and PIDA Gold 2024 awards.

**Only Good also carries the FernMark, the New Zealand Government's official mark of origin, which is granted to products that meet the country's origin-related eligibility criteria.** Apex Brands holds FernMark licence 100709.

In India, Only Good products are available through Kiwiyāna's Amazon India store and the brand's website, onlygood.in, with delivery services covering customers across the country.

{Funding Alert} Pet Food Startup Smylo Looks to Raise $3.2 Mn for Business Expansion

![Indian Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/art-logo.webp)

BY - [Indian Retailer Bureau](/author/indian-retailer-bureau)  
 Sub Editor  / 1 MIN READ

[Follow Us ![Indina Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/follow.webp)](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAiEJjETmBVGGR4AF2qcS42jEMqFAgKIhCYxE5gVRhkeABdqnEuNoxD?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN%3Aen)

![{Funding Alert} Pet Food Startup Smylo Looks to Raise $3.2 Mn for Business Expansion](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20Design%20-%202026-10-30T154121.031.jpg)

Smylo, a direct-to-consumer (D2C) cat food startup, is reportedly in advanced discussions to raise around Rs 30 crore (approximately $3.2 million) through a combination of equity and debt.

**The proposed funding round is expected to bring a new venture capital investor into the company's ownership structure, while existing investor DSG Consumer Partners is also considering additional participation.** Although the exact allocation between equity and debt remains unclear, sources indicated that equity would constitute the larger portion of the fundraise.

**Smylo plans to utilise the proposed investment to introduce new products, strengthen its research and development (R&D) capabilities and establish its own manufacturing facility.**

Founded in 2024 by former Titan Capital executives Abhishek Agrawal and Kartikeya Gupta, **Smylo manufactures cat food products that it claims are preservative-free, protein-rich and prepared using fresh meat.** Its product portfolio includes wet food, dry food and broths catering to both kittens and adult cats.

**The startup distributes its products through its direct-to-consumer website, e-commerce marketplaces and quick commerce platforms, including Blinkit and Zepto.**

**The founders disclosed that Smylo was generating average monthly sales of Rs 50-55 lakh.** At the time, approximately 80 percent of its revenue came from its website and e-commerce channels, while the remaining contribution came from quick commerce platforms.

**Before its appearance on Shark Tank India in early 2026, the startup had secured smaller funding rounds.** However, it did not reveal the cumulative amount raised through these investments.

**Smylo's proposed fundraise comes amid increasing investor interest in India's pet care industry, where startups operating across pet food, supplies and healthcare are attracting capital to support product development and business expansion.**

In September, D2C pet food company Lickicious raised Rs 19 crore through an equity and debt funding round led by Prath Ventures. The company planned to invest the proceeds in expanding its manufacturing operations, strengthening R&D and broadening its product portfolio and distribution channels.

**Earlier, in February, pet care marketplace Supertails secured $30 million in a Series C funding round.** The company intended to use the capital to expand its veterinary clinic network and strengthen its quick commerce infrastructure.

The growing investment activity reflects the expansion of India's pet care market, supported by increasing pet ownership and higher consumer spending on animal nutrition, food, and healthcare.

[Follow Us ![Indina Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/follow.webp)](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAiEJjETmBVGGR4AF2qcS42jEMqFAgKIhCYxE5gVRhkeABdqnEuNoxD?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN%3Aen)

![Skincare Startup CureSkin Cuts FY26 Loss to Rs 35 Cr](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20Design%20-%202026-10-29T152656.711.jpg)

Skincare and dermatology startup CureSkin reduced its net losses in FY26 as revenue growth and lower advertising and promotional expenditure improved its financial performance. **The Bengaluru-based company recorded a rise in income from product sales and services, alongside tighter control over several operating costs.**

**CureSkin's revenue from operations increased 27.9 percent to Rs 133 crore in FY26.** The company provides personalised skincare and [**haircare solutions**](https://www.indianretailer.com/article/tag/hair-care-product) through digital consultations and products recommended for individual skin and hair concerns. **Its business model combines product sales with dermatology-led services.**

**Product sales continued to account for the majority of CureSkin's operating revenue, contributing approximately 91 percent of the total.** Revenue from products grew 17.1 percent to Rs 120.6 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 103 crore in FY25.

**Revenue from services increased nearly ninefold to Rs 12.4 crore during the year, indicating a growing contribution from the segment, although product sales remained the company's primary source of income.** CureSkin also reported Rs 1 crore in other income, taking its total revenue to Rs 134 crore in FY26, against Rs 108 crore in the previous fiscal year.

**On the expenditure front, advertising and promotional costs declined 17.6 percent to Rs 61 crore in FY26 from Rs 74 crore in FY25.** The reduction in marketing expenditure helped lower the company's overall costs despite increases in certain operating expenses.

**The cost of materials consumed rose 15.4 percent to Rs 42 crore, broadly in line with the growth in product sales.** Employee benefit expenses declined 5.3 percent to Rs 23.6 crore from Rs 24.9 crore in the previous year.

**Transportation expenses increased 30 percent to Rs 13 crore, while legal and professional charges fell 36.5 percent to Rs 7.2 crore.** Miscellaneous expenses rose 14.8 percent to Rs 22.2 crore from Rs 19 crore in FY25.

**These changes in revenue and expenditure helped CureSkin narrow its net loss by 48.5 percent to Rs 35 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 68 crore in FY25.**

**The company's EBITDA margin improved to -21.81 percent from -60.94 percent a year earlier.** Its expenditure per rupee of operating revenue also declined to Rs 1.27 from Rs 1.69 in FY25, reflecting improved cost efficiency, although the business continued to operate at a loss.

As of March 2026, **CureSkin reported cash and bank balances of Rs 8 crore and current assets of Rs 40 crore, compared with Rs 72 crore in current assets a year earlier.**

The company has raised $26 million in funding to date, including a $20 million round led by HealthQuad. Its other investors include JSW, Khosla Ventures and Sharrp Ventures.

![{Funding Alert} D2C Nutrition Brand Ace Blend Raises $9.9 Mn in Series A2 Round](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20Design%20-%202026-10-29T124816.255.jpg)

Ace Blend, a direct-to-consumer (D2C) nutrition and dietary supplements brand, has raised $9.9 million (approximately Rs 95 crore) in a Series A2 funding round led by 3one4 Capital, with participation from existing investor Fireside Ventures.

**The company plans to deploy the fresh capital towards clinical trials, research and development (R&D), supply chain improvements, and the development of new nutrition formats.**

> **Shivam Hingorani, Founder and CEO, Ace Blend said,** “The first is clinical trials, which are going to be run by credible CROs (contract research organisations) and are intended to be published in peer-reviewed international journals. The second is cementing our moat as a business, which is our supply chain proficiency. The third is a robust testing mechanism that allows nutritional accuracy, pesticides, and heavy metals to be tested batch on batch without any human intervention.”

**The company also intends to conduct shelf-stability studies when products are introduced and again after six months.** According to Hingorani, these studies will help establish long-term safety data for its product portfolio.

**Emphasising the importance of scientific validation in the nutritional supplements industry, Hingorani said, “Trust is not enough”.**

**Founded in 2018 by Hingorani, Ace Blend was joined by Saif Mehkri as co-founder in 2022.** The company offers dietary supplements across categories such as heart health, brain health, sleep, recovery, gut health, strength and immunity. Its portfolio comprises approximately 14 stock-keeping units (SKUs), including plant-based protein powders, superfood mixes and functional health supplements.

**Ace Blend sells its products through its website and online commerce platforms, including Amazon, Flipkart, Zepto and Blinkit.** Hingorani said the company's website contributes around 50 percent of its revenue, while the remaining share comes from marketplaces and other e-commerce channels.

According to Hingorani, **the startup recorded 300 percent growth in FY26 and has a repeat purchase rate of nearly 48 percent.** It is targeting annual recurring revenue (ARR) of Rs 250-300 crore over the next 12-18 months, with profitability also within its plans.

The company is looking to strengthen its supply chain by procuring raw materials from multiple countries. Its vertically integrated operating model covers ingredient sourcing, formulation, and manufacturing. **Ace Blend is also working towards implementing automated testing to assess nutritional accuracy, pesticide residues, and heavy metals in every batch.**

The startup is developing several new products, including a formulation designed with a gut-health specialist to address leaky gut, a blend of natural nutrients intended to reduce inflammation, an eye-health supplement and a fibre-based product for gut health, Hingorani said.

**The funding comes amid growing consumer interest in preventive healthcare and dietary supplements in India.** Increasing awareness of nutrition and the role of supplements in managing chronic conditions has also attracted investor attention to the sector. **Earlier this month, D2C supplement brand The Stack raised Rs 21.5 crore to expand its product portfolio and invest in research and development.**

**The brand's visual identity centres on casual streetwear with an experimental approach to design.** Its use of alien-inspired graphics and outer-space motifs adds a distinctive element to relaxed clothing styles, offering an alternative to conventional everyday fashion.

**Patani's entry into the clothing segment marks an expansion of her professional activities beyond acting.** Through DZ, she is bringing her interest in unconventional aesthetics into a fashion business, with oversized silhouettes and graphic-led designs forming the core of the brand's identity.

The launch also reflects the growing intersection of celebrity-led businesses and fashion, with public figures using their personal style and audience reach to introduce apparel brands. **DZ enters this segment with a focus on relaxed streetwear, distinctive graphics and designs inspired by space and futuristic themes.**

Bengaluru-based orthopaedic products startup Lumov is in discussions to raise Rs 32 crore in a funding round led by Peak XV Partners. **The proposed round is expected to include participation from the founders of personal care brand Minimalist and luggage brand Mokobara, along with early-stage venture capital firm Panthera Peak Ventures.**

Founded in 2024 by Saumaric Dangwal and Ankit Gupta, Lumov designs and manufactures orthopaedic products and orthoses for post-surgical recovery, rehabilitation, and pain management. **The company operates in the healthcare products segment, addressing requirements related to physical recovery and musculoskeletal support.**

**The startup plans to use the proposed funding to support its operations.** Further details about the funding round, including the final investment amount, valuation, and the individual contributions of participating investors, have not been disclosed.

**Lumov's product portfolio focuses on orthopaedic support solutions used during recovery and rehabilitation.** Orthoses are external devices designed to support, align or protect parts of the body and can be used to assist movement or manage specific musculoskeletal conditions. **Such products are commonly used in rehabilitation programmes and post-operative care, depending on patients' clinical requirements.**

**The company's focus on orthopaedic products places it within a healthcare segment that serves patients requiring support during recovery from surgery, injuries and other conditions affecting movement.** Its business model combines product design and manufacturing to address these needs.

The proposed investment would provide Lumov with additional capital to support its ongoing business activities as it develops its presence in the orthopaedic healthcare products market. **However, the company has not shared specific details regarding plans for product expansion, manufacturing capacity, or geographical reach as part of the proposed funding.**

**The participation of Peak XV Partners, the founders of Minimalist and Mokobara, and Panthera Peak Ventures would bring together institutional venture capital and entrepreneurs associated with consumer-focused businesses.** The outcome of the funding discussions and the company's subsequent operational plans will depend on the completion and terms of the proposed transaction.

Skincare brand CHOSEN has raised an extension to its Series A funding round from Avnish Chhabria and Saurabh Kapoor, founders of Wellbeing Nutrition, as it looks to strengthen its research and development (R&D) capabilities and expand its product portfolio.

**The Chennai-based startup previously raised $5 million in a Series A funding round led by Fireside Ventures in May 2026.** The round also included participation from BOLD, L’Oréal’s corporate venture capital fund, Alkemi Growth Capital, and other angel investors. In 2024, CHOSEN secured $1.2 million in an angel funding round.

**The latest funding will support the development of its R&D capabilities and expand its formulation pipeline across topical skincare and nutraceuticals**. The company will focus on clinical validation and dermatological research as part of its product development strategy.

**Founded in 2020 by Renita Rajan, CHOSEN develops skincare products for melanin-rich Indian skin.** Its product development approach is based on the science of the exposome, which studies how environmental factors influence skin health. **The brand focuses on four aspects of ageing: pigmentation, skin texture, facial contour and hair ageing.**

**As part of its expansion plans, CHOSEN intends to establish a Centre of Excellence to bring dermatologists into its product development and research processes.** The company also plans to strengthen its R&D, brand and growth teams to support its next phase of business expansion.

**CHOSEN offers more than 50 products across skincare, haircare, body care and nutraceuticals.** Its products are prescribed by over 2,000 doctors. In 2026, the company introduced CHOSEN Sculpt, which it identifies as India's first topical lower face contouring serum. **The product is supported by a 12-week clinical study involving Indian women, published in the Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology.**

**The brand sells through its official website and online platforms, including Amazon, Myntra, Swiggy, FirstClub and Distacart.** Its distribution network covers most serviceable pin codes across India. Key markets include Chennai, Coimbatore, Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Mumbai, Delhi NCR, Pune, Ahmedabad and Goa.

Beyond India, CHOSEN serves customers in international markets, including the US, the UK, Australia, Canada, the UAE, Singapore, France, Sweden, Portugal, the Czech Republic, Hong Kong and Thailand.

![{Funding Alert} Preventive Healthcare Startup Cent Raises $15 Mn in Series A Round](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20Design%20-%202026-10-27T144107.040.jpg)

Preventive healthcare startup Cent has raised $15 million in a Series A funding round co-led by Blume Ventures and South Park Commons. **The company has also acquired Medsee, an artificial intelligence (AI)-powered radiology platform, to strengthen its technology capabilities.**

**The funding round also saw participation from individual investors Arun Sarin, Srinivas Narayanan, Sharath Narayana, Aprameya Radhakrishna and Krishan Sridhar.**

Founded by Shashank ND, who previously established healthcare platform Practo, Cent focuses on detecting diseases at an early stage using medical imaging, biomarkers and AI. **The company aims to identify potential health risks before they progress into more serious conditions.**

**Over the past year, approximately 10,000 people have undergone screening through Cent's protocol.** The company reported that one in four individuals had findings requiring medical attention, while one in 40 needed an immediate consultation with a doctor.

**Cent's screening protocol combines full-body magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), low-dose computed tomography (CT) scans, dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA), electrocardiograms (ECG), echocardiograms (ECHO) and more than 100 biomarkers.** The tests are conducted in a single session lasting approximately two hours.

**The startup operates its own screening centres in Bengaluru, Mumbai and Delhi-NCR, in addition to its existing network of partner diagnostic laboratories.**

**The newly raised capital will be allocated towards investments in medical hardware, AI capabilities and clinical research.** The acquisition of Medsee is also expected to strengthen Cent's AI capabilities, according to Shashank.

**The company has set a target of conducting 10 million scans by 2035 and aims to help save one million lives through early disease detection.**

**Cent is targeting gaps in India's healthcare system, particularly the late diagnosis of noncommunicable diseases.** India has approximately 101 million people living with diabetes and 136 million with prediabetes. An estimated 315 million people in the country also have hypertension.

**The funding and acquisition come as Cent seeks to expand its preventive healthcare services and develop technology-led screening solutions.**

In September 2026, Practo elevated Shashank ND to the positions of managing director and executive chairman, while Jagnoor Singh was appointed chief executive officer (CEO).

Snack brand Troovy has raised Rs 100 crore in a Series B funding round led by Fireside Ventures, with participation from Sharrp Ventures and other investors. **The company plans to use the capital to strengthen its product development capabilities, increase manufacturing capacity, and expand its distribution network.**

**Troovy was reportedly looking to raise up to Rs 200 crore in a Series B round.**

Founded in 2023 by Aditya Mukherjee and Mansi Baranwal, Troovy offers a range of food products, including snacks, sauces, spreads and millet pasta. **The brand focuses on developing convenient food options for children and families using selected ingredients.**

**The fresh funding will support research and development (R&D), manufacturing expansion, and distribution growth across quick-commerce platforms and offline retail channels.** According to the company, the proceeds will also help accelerate its Build Together model.

**Troovy develops products using feedback from parents and insights into children's food preferences.** Its approach focuses on product innovation to make alternative food choices more accessible to families. The company said its vacuum-cooked potato chips contain 10 percent to 12 percent oil, compared with 35 percent to 40 percent in mainstream chips. **Its portfolio also includes ketchup and seasonings for children that are made without synthetic additives or preservatives.**

**The latest round follows Troovy's earlier fundraising activities.** In January 2026, the company raised $5 million in a Series A round led by Fireside Ventures and Sharrp Ventures, with participation from existing investors Spring Marketing Capital and Veltis Capital. **Before that, it secured Rs 20 crore, equivalent to approximately $2.3 million, in a pre-Series A round led by Fireside Ventures in May 2025.**

**Troovy operates in the children's health food segment, competing with brands such as Slurrp Farm, Timios and The Mumum Co.** The broader better-for-you food category has attracted brands including Open Secret and Beyond Snack, which are expanding through direct-to-consumer (D2C), e-commerce, quick-commerce and offline retail channels.

The latest investment positions Troovy to expand its operations and strengthen its presence in India's growing better-for-you snacking market.

Luxury watch brand Rotoris has secured Rs 70 crore (approximately $8.5 million) in a Series A funding round led by Blume Ventures. **The round also included investments from 9Unicorns, Centricity and several family offices, including those of Diwakar Goel, Atul Singh and Adhiraj Burman.** Actor and television host Rannvijay Singha also participated in the funding round.

![{Funding Alert} BioStack Secures $9.5 Mn Seed Funding for Healthcare Data Platform](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20Design%20-%202026-10-26T175757.437.jpg)

Healthcare technology startup BioStack has raised $9.5 million in a seed funding round led by Peak XV, Afore Capital, DCVC, Emerson Collective, SV Angel, Verdict Capital, Streamlined Ventures, and Y Combinator. **The company plans to use the fresh capital to expand internationally, develop its technology and strengthen its engineering and research teams.**

**BioStack is building a healthcare data infrastructure network across the United States, India, Brazil and Argentina, with access to more than 100 million de-identified patient records.** The platform aims to connect fragmented clinical information from hospitals and healthcare systems to create longitudinal patient records that bring together medical histories, laboratory results, imaging reports, medications, treatment records, and patient outcomes.

**Founded by Sanat Mishra, BioStack develops proprietary datasets from de-identified clinical information to support medical research, drug development and the training and evaluation of healthcare artificial intelligence (AI) models.**

**Its technology is designed for applications including disease modelling, biomarker discovery, patient stratification, and treatment response analysis.** By consolidating information from multiple healthcare sources, the company aims to make clinical data more accessible for research and the development of healthcare technologies.

**BioStack said it has aggregated several hundred thousand X-rays, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans and computed tomography (CT) scans, alongside millions of telehealth audio transcripts and other clinical records.**

**The company's operations also extend to patient support initiatives in India, where it is helping connect cancer patients with an investigational cancer vaccine programme.**

**BioStack's platform incorporates workflows tailored to individual healthcare providers and their data privacy protocols.** This approach is intended to accommodate differences in how healthcare organisations manage clinical information while enabling the use of de-identified data for research and technology development.

**With the latest funding, BioStack plans to advance its data infrastructure, expand its international presence and increase investment in research and engineering.** Its focus remains on connecting fragmented healthcare information and developing datasets that can support clinical research, pharmaceutical development, and AI applications across healthcare systems.

![{Funding Alert} Performance Wear Brand ReplyAll Raises Rs 9.7 Cr in Funding Round](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20Design%20-%202026-10-26T113536.112.jpg)

ReplyAll, an everyday performance wear brand founded by Rushabh Sanghavi in 2025, has raised Rs 9.7 crore in a funding round led by Sadev Ventures and Atom XVII. **Other participants included ISV, represented by Jivraj Singh Sachar, Long View Ventures, existing investors Sparrow and Antler, and angel investors.**

**The company will use the funds for fabric research and development, product design, category expansion, and strengthening its retail and community presence.**

**ReplyAll develops clothing for consumers balancing work, travel, sports, and everyday activities.** Its product strategy combines versatile designs, functional details, and material innovation to create garments that transition across different settings.

**Harmind Singh has joined the company as Co-Founder and Chief Marketing Officer (CMO).** He will oversee brand, marketing, creative, and product design. Singh brings two decades of experience across design, branding, and consumer technology, having held senior leadership roles at PhonePe, BookMyShow, and Uber.

> **Rushabh Sanghavi, Founder and CEO, ReplyAll shared,** "Almost everyone in urban India is living several lives at once. A day can move from a hot commute to an air-conditioned office, an evening game, and dinner with friends. Yet we still tend to dress for each of those moments separately. We believe everyday clothing should work harder for the life people actually lead. That means getting the design right, understanding how materials feel and perform, and building functionality into clothes people want to wear every day. This funding allows us to deepen that work and bring the same thinking into more categories."

**The brand's material platforms include Temperform, used in its Coolest Tee to help manage heat, and Flexknit, which provides stretch and wrinkle resistance in trousers.** Its first three products, the Coolest Tee, All-In Pants and Stepwise Tee, have each sold out. ReplyAll also reported monthly revenue growth over the past seven months, with repeat customers contributing 40 percent of revenue.

> **Dhruv Dhanraj Bahl, Founder and Managing Partner of Sadev Ventures shared,** "In consumer, the moats that last aren't visible on the rack - they're woven into the fabric. ReplyAll understood that from day one. Their materials-first approach is hard to copy compounds over time, and the early traction shows consumers can feel the difference. That's why we backed them."

> **Harsh Kapadia, Founder and Managing Partner of Atom XVII stated,** "We look for categories before they become obvious. The Indian Consumer now has several more occasions, outings, and experiences to spend on! And we want to dress for any and all occasions but still don’t have the time, so we need our outfits to do more. ReplyAll has the product foundation to become the everyday wardrobe for that shift."

> "Every product we make has to answer two questions: does it look good enough to want, and does it work well enough to need? If it only does one, it isn't enough. We want ReplyAll to be known for that point of view, and to build a brand and community people want to be part of," **said Harmind Singh, CMO and Founder, ReplyAll.**

**With the fresh funding, ReplyAll plans to expand its product categories and strengthen its materials-led approach to everyday performance wear.**

Wellbeing Nutrition Revenue Doubles in FY26, Expenses Rise to Rs 338 Cr

![Indian Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/art-logo.webp)

BY - [Indian Retailer Bureau](/author/indian-retailer-bureau)  
 Sub Editor  / 1 MIN READ

[Follow Us ![Indina Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/follow.webp)](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAiEJjETmBVGGR4AF2qcS42jEMqFAgKIhCYxE5gVRhkeABdqnEuNoxD?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN%3Aen)

![Wellbeing Nutrition Revenue Doubles in FY26, Expenses Rise to Rs 338 Cr](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-10-23T120138.347.jpg)

Clean-label nutraceutical brand Wellbeing Nutrition more than doubled its operating revenue to Rs 244 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 118 crore in FY25, while its net loss increased 2.4 times to Rs 92 crore. **The financial performance follows pharmaceutical major USV’s acquisition of a 79 percent stake in the company.**

**Wellbeing Nutrition’s revenue growth was driven by sales across its nutraceutical and wellness product portfolio.** Founded in 2019, the company offers vitamins, minerals, protein, collagen, omega supplements and other wellness products. **It sells through its website, online marketplaces and** [**offline retail channels**](https://www.indianretailer.com/article/tag/offline-retail)**, with operations extending to markets such as the US, UK and UAE.**

**Product sales accounted for the company’s entire operating revenue in** [**FY26**](https://www.indianretailer.com/news/tag/fy26-report)**.** Its portfolio includes collagen supplements, oral strips, marine collagen, slow-release capsules and effervescent tablets.

**However, rising marketing and operating costs contributed to the increase in expenditure.** Advertising and promotional spending rose 78.7 percent to Rs 109 crore in FY26 from Rs 61 crore in the previous fiscal year, accounting for around 32 percent of total expenditure. **The cost of materials consumed also more than doubled to Rs 106 crore during the year.**

**Other expenses, including freight, commissions, legal fees and overheads, further increased the company’s cost base.** Consequently, total expenditure climbed 115.3 percent to Rs 338 crore in FY26 from Rs 157 crore in FY25.

**Wellbeing Nutrition’s net loss widened to Rs 92 crore from Rs 38 crore a year earlier.** The loss included an employee stock ownership plan (ESOP) expense of approximately Rs 51 crore. **Excluding this expense, the company’s loss would have been around Rs 40 crore.**

**Despite the higher reported loss, its operating EBITDA loss, excluding ESOP expenses, improved to 13.4 percent of revenue in FY26 from 22.5 percent in FY25.** At the unit economics level, Wellbeing Nutrition spent Rs 1.39 for every rupee earned in operating revenue during the fiscal year.

**In February 2026, pharmaceutical company USV agreed to acquire a 79 percent stake in Wellbeing Nutrition at a valuation of Rs 1,583 crore.** The transaction also offers existing investors an opportunity to exit partially or fully.

**The acquisition is among the notable transactions in India’s direct-to-consumer (D2C) sector in 2026.** In February, Mumbai-based consumer goods company Marico acquired a 60 percent stake in plant-based protein startup Cosmix at an equity valuation of Rs 375 crore.

![Ultraviolette Introduces X-47 Venom With 12 kW DC Fast Charging](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-10-23T104959.331.jpg)

Bengaluru-based electric mobility startup Ultraviolette Automotive has introduced the X-47 Venom [**electric motorcycle in India**](https://www.indianretailer.com/news/tag/electric-vehicle) at an introductory price of Rs 2.65 lakh. Built on the company’s new 100V VX-100 platform, the motorcycle is scheduled for deliveries from November 2026. **Bookings open on October 22, with the introductory price available to the first 5,000 customers.** The model will be available across India through Ultraviolette’s UV Space Stations.

The X-47 Venom offers an IDC-certified range of 343 km, peak power of 30 kW (40 hp), and a top speed of 155 kmph. It accelerates from 0 to 60 kmph in 2.7 seconds and from 0 to 100 kmph in 5.9 seconds. According to the company, **the** [**motorcycle**](https://www.indianretailer.com/news/tag/motorcycle) **delivers 550 Nm of wheel torque and has a kerb weight of 180 kg, up to 20 kg lower than the previous-generation platform.**

The electric motorcycle supports 12 kW DC fast charging and comes with a 1.6 kW onboard charger. **Ultraviolette claims it is the only electric two-wheeler in India to support 12 kW DC fast charging.**

> “The X-47 Venom brings these advances to life, combining distinctive design with deeper engineering capabilities and technology that enhances the riding experience,” **said Narayan Subramaniam, CEO and co-founder, Ultraviolette.**

**The VX-100 architecture integrates the company’s SRB-11 battery technology, UV LIGHTFURY motor, and next-generation motor control unit.** Ultraviolette said the battery offers up to 20 percent higher energy density and twice the cooling performance, while its thermal management system is designed to dissipate heat up to 50 percent faster.

**Safety features include a pyro-fuse that isolates the electrical circuit within microseconds when a critical fault is detected, alongside a battery management system that monitors cell-level voltage, temperature and current.** The motorcycle also features a 77 GHz rear radar system under UV Hypersense technology, supporting blind-spot monitoring, lane-change assistance, overtake alerts and rear-collision warnings.

**Other features include a seven-inch TFT touchscreen, cruise control, park assist with a rear-camera feed, Mappls-integrated navigation and VIOLETTE A.I. connectivity.** The company has also introduced B-MAX, a reusable rider safety vest that it claims provides 86 percent force attenuation and can be reused up to five times.

**Founded in 2016 by Narayan Subramaniam and CTO and co-founder Niraj Rajmohan, Ultraviolette develops electric vehicle platforms and battery technologies.** The company said it has expanded its presence to 20 countries across Europe and plans to showcase the X-47 Venom at EICMA 2026 in Milan, Italy, on November 3.

![Innovist Revenue Rises to Rs 685.7 Cr Amid Higher Marketing Costs](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-10-22T174940.944.jpg)

Beauty and personal care company Innovist nearly tripled its operating revenue in FY26, supported by higher product sales across its distribution channels. **The company also recorded an 87 percent increase in net profit during the financial year, although rising expenditure on advertising, promotions and sales commissions added to its operating costs.**

**Innovist, operated by Onesto Labs, reported revenue from operations of Rs 685.7 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 246.7 crore in FY25.**

**The company operates in the cosmetics and beauty products segment, manufacturing products in India and selling primarily through online marketplaces, its own website and third-party offline retail outlets.**

**Product sales remained the principal contributor to its operating revenue, generating Rs 676.3 crore in FY26 against Rs 239.1 crore in the previous financial year.** Other operating revenue, which includes income from shipping and scrap sales, stood at Rs 9.4 crore during FY26.

**The company's revenue growth was accompanied by a substantial increase in spending on customer acquisition and distribution.** Advertising and promotional expenses rose more than threefold to Rs 262 crore in FY26 from Rs 84.2 crore in FY25. These expenses accounted for approximately 40 percent of the company's total costs.

**Commissions paid to sole selling agents also increased significantly, reaching Rs 92 crore during FY26 compared with Rs 15 crore a year earlier.** Meanwhile, the cost of materials consumed rose to Rs 162 crore from Rs 79 crore, reflecting the expansion in business activity. Employee benefit expenses more than doubled to Rs 39 crore from Rs 19 crore.

**As a result, Innovist's total expenses increased to Rs 662 crore in FY26 from Rs 250 crore in FY25.** Despite the higher expenditure, the company reported a profit before tax of Rs 30.5 crore, compared with a loss before tax of Rs 55 lakh in the previous fiscal year.

**The company's tax expense reached Rs 8.9 crore in FY26, including a deferred tax expense of Rs 7.8 crore.** After accounting for taxes, Innovist reported a net profit of Rs 21.5 crore for the year, representing an 87 percent increase over FY25.

**Its balance sheet also reflected a current asset base of Rs 303 crore at the end of FY26, including cash and bank balances of Rs 81 crore.**

**Innovist's financial performance indicates that the company has expanded its sales while maintaining profitability.** However, the increase in advertising and promotional expenditure highlights the importance of improving returns on marketing investments as the business grows.

Bengaluru-based direct-to-consumer (D2C) skincare brand Deconstruct reported revenue of Rs 165 crore in FY26, marking a 30 percent year-on-year increase from Rs 127 crore in FY25. **The company's operating revenue has grown 25-fold over three years, although higher expenditure on marketing and business operations pushed it into a net loss of Rs 5.4 crore during the financial year ended March 2026.**

**Deconstruct continued to expand its business while maintaining a relatively limited loss compared with its revenue.** However, the company's total expenses increased faster than its revenue, affecting its overall profitability.

**Founded by Malini Adapureddy, Deconstruct develops skincare products for different skin types, including sensitive skin.** Its portfolio includes face care, body care, lip care, and hair care products for men and women. The brand operates in India's competitive D2C beauty and personal care market.

**The company's expansion was accompanied by higher spending on advertising and promotional activities.** These expenses increased 72.5 percent to Rs 69 crore in FY26, accounting for approximately 40 percent of its total expenditure. **The increase reflects the cost of marketing and customer acquisition as the brand expands its market presence.**

**Procurement expenses also rose 39.3 percent to Rs 39 crore during FY26, in line with the company's growing business**. Additional costs associated with transportation, freight, legal services and other operational overheads further contributed to expenditure.

**Deconstruct's total expenses increased 48.7 percent to Rs 174 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 117 crore in the previous financial year.** With expenditure rising faster than operating revenue, the company recorded a net loss of Rs 5.4 crore, reversing the net profit of Rs 10 crore reported in FY25.

**The company's EBITDA margin stood at -5.61 percent, while its return on capital employed (ROCE) was -13.81 percent.** At the operating level, Deconstruct spent approximately Rs 1.05 for every rupee of operating revenue generated during FY26.

**Deconstruct has received investments from Kalaari Capital, DSG Consumer Partners, V3 Ventures, and BOLD, the venture capital fund associated with L'Oréal.** The funding has supported the company's business growth and expansion.

**The brand competes with established players in India's D2C skincare segment, including Minimalist, The Derma Co, Foxtale and Dot & Key.** As competition intensifies, managing customer acquisition costs and encouraging repeat purchases will remain important to sustaining growth.

**Deconstruct's financial performance highlights its ability to expand revenue while facing pressure on profitability.** Advertising and promotional spending represents a substantial share of its costs, making the conversion of marketing investments into repeat purchases and sustained sales a key factor in its future performance.

**The next phase of growth will depend on the company's ability to improve cost efficiency while expanding its customer base.** The brand's progress towards profitability, alongside its ability to sustain revenue growth beyond the Rs 100 crore to Rs 150 crore range, will be important indicators of its financial trajectory.

![Indian Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/art-logo.webp)

BY - [Indian Retailer Bureau](/author/indian-retailer-bureau)  
 Sub Editor  / 1 MIN READ

[Follow Us ![Indina Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/follow.webp)](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAiEJjETmBVGGR4AF2qcS42jEMqFAgKIhCYxE5gVRhkeABdqnEuNoxD?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN%3Aen)

![{Funding Alert} Even Healthcare Raises $50 Mn in Series B Funding Led by Khosla Ventures](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-10-22T145735.821.jpg)

Bengaluru-based managed care startup Even Healthcare has raised $50 million (approximately Rs 475 crore) in a Series B funding round led by existing investor Khosla Ventures, with participation from Alpha Wave. **The all-equity primary funding round takes the company's total capital raised to more than $120 million.**

**Even Healthcare plans to use the fresh capital primarily to expand its hospital network in Bengaluru.** The company aims to open another hospital by the end of 2026, followed by three additional facilities by the end of FY27. **It currently operates two multispeciality hospitals, located on Race Course Road and in HBR Layout.**

The startup intends to expand into other cities after establishing a stronger presence in Bengaluru. “We want to make sure that Bengaluru patients and members are pretty well served,” **stated Mayank Banerjee, co-founder, Even Healthcare.**

Even Healthcare said its valuation has tripled since its previous fundraise 18 months ago, although it has not disclosed its current valuation. **Earlier this year, the company raised $20 million to expand its hospital network and develop new facilities.**

**Founded in 2020 by Mayank Banerjee, Matilde Giglio and Alessandro Ialongo, Even Healthcare operates an integrated managed care model that combines preventive healthcare, outpatient consultations, diagnostic services, insurance access, hospitalisation and post-discharge recovery. T**he company aims to manage patients' health across different stages of care rather than focusing solely on individual hospital visits.

**Its services include telemedicine consultations, at-home blood tests, medical guidance and cashless hospitalisation through insurance partners.** The startup also employs salaried doctors whose compensation is not tied to the number of procedures performed or the revenue generated. **Instead, it evaluates doctors based on patient outcomes, recovery periods and hospital readmissions.**

**Banerjee said approximately 85 to 90 percent of Even members living near one of its Bengaluru hospitals choose the startup for their healthcare needs.**

**The company also uses an artificial intelligence-based quality monitoring system to assess medical cases against clinical protocols in real time.** It recently introduced Even Spotlight, a dashboard designed to track clinical outcomes and patient-reported metrics.

**Unplanned readmissions under programmes operated with insurance partners remain below 1 percent, compared with an industry range of 8 to 15 percent.** Even also reported that average hospital stays were 40 percent shorter. Additionally, the company said its proactive healthcare programmes helped more than 200 members avoid hospitalisation, resulting in estimated savings of Rs 15 crore to Rs 16 crore.

**Even Healthcare claims to serve more than 2.5 lakh members across 10 cities, with its membership base tripling over the past year.**

**The latest funding comes as the startup continues to shift towards a hospital-led healthcare model.** The new investment is expected to support the company's hospital expansion strategy, strengthen its integrated care delivery model, and help establish its presence in Bengaluru before entering additional markets.

![{Funding Alert} CureBay Raises Rs 100 Cr in Pre-Series C Round Led by IvyCap Ventures](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-10-22T125815.489.jpg)

CureBay, a rural healthcare startup, has raised approximately Rs 100 crore in a Pre-Series C funding round led by IvyCap Ventures. **The funding combines equity investments from new and existing investors with debt financing, providing the company with additional capital to expand its healthcare network and strengthen its technology infrastructure.**

**The round includes Rs 69 crore in equity funding from IvyCap Ventures and existing investors, alongside more than Rs 30 crore in debt secured from Trifecta Capital, Alteria Capital and VentureSoul Partners.**

**CureBay plans to use the fresh capital to expand its operations across India, including entering Andhra Pradesh.** The company will also invest in technology and artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance health screening, generate patient insights, and support clinical decision-making.

**Founded in 2021 by Priyadarshi Mohapatra, Shobhan Mahapatra and Sanjay Swain, CureBay focuses on improving access to healthcare in underserved and rural communities through a network of technology-enabled clinics.** Its services cover doctor consultations, medicines, diagnostic testing, surgery facilitation and annual health memberships.

**The company currently operates more than 250 clinics across seven states. Its network is supported by over 1,800 Swasthya Mitras, 530 trained clinical staff, 230 doctor partners and more than 210 partner hospitals and laboratories.** CureBay has served over 17 lakh patients and organises more than 400 health camps every month.

**The startup follows a six-layer rural healthcare model that integrates physical clinics, community health workers, a digital platform, AI-powered screening, a 24/7 command centre and CureBay Kavach.** The model combines in-person healthcare delivery with digital tools and community-level support to improve access to medical services in areas with limited healthcare infrastructure.

**Alongside its private healthcare operations, CureBay collaborates with government bodies on healthcare delivery initiatives.** The company has also been named the healthcare partner for Samriddhi Kendra, a Government of India initiative.

**The latest funding follows CureBay's previous capital raise of $21 million in a Series B round in May 2025.** The round was led by Bertelsmann India Investments, with participation from existing investor Elevar Equity and British International Investment.

**With the new funding, CureBay plans to widen its geographical reach while strengthening its technology-led healthcare delivery model.** Its expansion strategy centres on increasing access to medical consultations, diagnostics and other healthcare services in underserved regions, while using AI and digital infrastructure to support patient screening and clinical processes.

![{Funding Alert} Chapter Home Raises Rs 63 Cr to Expand Home and Kitchen Brands](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-10-22T123131.888.jpg)

Chapter Home, a consumer brand company focused on home and kitchen products, has raised Rs 63 crore in a funding round backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Stride Ventures, influencer Tanmay Bhat, and a group of family offices. **The investment comprises a combination of equity and debt and values the company at nearly Rs 1,000 crore.**

**The company plans to deploy the fresh capital towards product development, category expansion, technology investments, brand building, and strengthening its distribution network.** It is also preparing to establish its first physical retail touchpoints as it looks to expand its presence beyond online sales.

Founded in 2025 by Nitin Chugh, Akarsh Bharadwaj, Shrey Mittal, Dhiraj Jain and Dheeraj Goyal, Chapter Home is building consumer brands across the home and kitchen segment. **Its portfolio spans categories such as bed and table linen, cookware, home décor, and small kitchen appliances.**

**Before establishing Chapter Home, the founders were part of the founding and leadership team at PharmEasy.** Their experience in building and managing a consumer-facing business forms part of the team's background as it develops its presence in the home and kitchen market.

**Chapter Home follows a shared-platform model across its brands, bringing together sourcing, supply chain management, content, technology and distribution.** This structure is intended to support operations across multiple product categories while enabling the company to build and scale individual brands using common resources.

**Technology is another component of the company's operating model.** Chapter Home uses artificial intelligence (AI) for several functions, including product cataloguing, content creation, demand forecasting, product assortment planning, customer targeting and retention. **These applications can support inventory planning, improve product discovery, and help the company understand customer preferences as its portfolio expands.**

**The company entered the market with home furnishings through HOKIPO, its online home furnishing brand.** The brand serves as the starting point for Chapter Home's broader plans to establish a presence across the home and kitchen products market.

**Going forward, Chapter Home intends to expand into additional categories while building a multi-channel distribution network.** Its sales strategy includes online marketplaces, quick commerce platforms, its direct-to-consumer (D2C) channel, and offline retail stores.

**The planned entry into physical retail is expected to add another sales channel to the company's existing online operations.** By combining digital platforms with offline distribution, Chapter Home aims to broaden consumer access to its products as it expands into new segments.

![{Funding Alert} Battery Smart Secures Nearly Rs 100 Cr to Expand EV Battery-Swapping Network](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-10-17T184318.248.jpg)

Battery-swapping startup Battery Smart has secured nearly Rs 100 crore from existing investor Ecosystem Integrity Fund as it prepares to expand its battery-swapping infrastructure for electric two- and three-wheelers. **The latest investment will support the company's expansion strategy and the scaling of its operations.**  
  
**Battery Smart allotted 18,000 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 54,407 per share, raising approximately Rs 98 crore from the investor.**

**The funding round appears to be ongoing, with the Gurugram-based startup expected to raise additional capital in multiple tranches.**

In August 2026, Battery Smart raised Rs 185.5 crore ($19.5 million) in a Series C funding round led by existing investor Rising Tide Ventures. **Ecosystem Integrity Fund and Blume Ventures also participated in the round.**

**The latest transaction values the company at approximately Rs 4,170 crore ($440 million) on a post-money basis.** The fresh capital is expected to be directed towards business expansion, capital expenditure, working capital requirements, and general corporate purposes,

**Founded in 2020, Battery Smart operates a battery-swapping network catering to electric two- and three-wheelers.** Through its battery-as-a-service (BaaS) model, the company enables users to exchange discharged batteries for charged ones instead of purchasing batteries upfront. The model is particularly relevant for gig economy drivers and other commercial users who depend on electric vehicles for their livelihoods.

**With this latest investment, Battery Smart has raised nearly $52 million through debt and equity transactions in 2026.** Its fundraising activity this year includes $7.2 million in a pre-Series C round, $15 million in debt financing from Mirova, and the $19.5 million Series C round completed in August.

**The company has raised more than $221 million to date, with investors including Tiger Global, Blume Ventures, and Ecosystem Integrity Fund.**

**Battery Smart has also reported improved financial performance. Revenue increased 43.8 percent to Rs 358 crore in FY26 from Rs 249 crore in FY25.** Meanwhile, its losses declined 12.8 percent year-on-year to Rs 23.55 crore, indicating an improvement in its financial performance as the business continues to expand.

![{Funding Alert} Healthcare Startup Vitonnix Raises Seed Funding from Inflection Point Ventures](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-10-17T174532.008.jpg)

Vitonnix, a preventive healthcare startup developed in the UK, has secured its first institutional funding in a seed round led by Inflection Point Ventures.

**The round also attracted investments from practising doctors and celebrities, including Bollywood actors Riteish Deshmukh and Boman Irani, singer Jaspinder Narula, and film producer Madhu Mantena.**

**The startup will utilise the proceeds to strengthen its senior management team, establish a consumer growth engine, broaden its distribution network and expand into new international markets.**

Vitonnix was founded by Dr Prashant Jindal, a UK-based refractive eye surgeon, dermatologist Dr Deepti Jindal, and oral surgeon Dr Rajesh Handa. **The company develops nutritional sprays designed for sublingual delivery.**

**The startup aims to offer an alternative to conventional supplement delivery methods by focusing on nutrient absorption through the oral mucosa.** Its SubliSpray range comprises nutritional formulations designed with an emphasis on ingredient compatibility, dosage accuracy, taste, and stability.

According to the company, **the platform is the outcome of more than a decade of research and development, supported by three completed clinical studies involving key formulations.**

While Vitonnix was initially developed in the UK, India serves as its research, formulation, and manufacturing base. Its global operations are managed from London and Birmingham.

**The company states that its precision spray systems are engineered in Germany. It has also filed patent applications covering its bottle designs and formulations.**

Vitonnix has undertaken product registration, regulatory filing, and market-entry initiatives across India, the UK, the US, and the UAE. In the Indian market, the startup received early support from the Tata Group and later introduced a co-branded product range within the Tata ecosystem.

**The company is preparing to roll out its first 10 products, with a UK launch planned for 2026. The proposed market entry includes a potential launch through British retailer Boots.**

In addition to human nutrition, Vitonnix has ventured into the pet nutrition segment with Vetonnix, a range of oral nutritional sprays developed for companion animals. **The initial lineup covers several needs, including skin and coat health, calming support, multivitamins, growth and development, and bone and joint care.**

![{Funding Alert} Kitchen Secret Secures Fresh Capital to Expand Ready-to-Cook Sauce Business](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/The%20campaign%E2%80%99s%20%E2%80%98UA%E2%80%99%20concept%20draws%20inspiration%20from%20film%20certification%20terminology%2C%20using%20it%20to%20represent%20the%20unrestricted%20spirit%20of%20childhood.%20%285%29.jpg)

Kitchen Secret, a preservative-free brand offering ready-to-eat and ready-to-cook sauces, has secured Rs 1.14 crore in its first external funding round. **The investment was led by BeyondSeed, with participation from angel investors. The brand was founded by mother-son duo Renuka Kedia and Manav Kedia.**

The company plans to deploy the fresh capital towards marketing, inventory expansion, wider distribution across quick-commerce platforms and the growth of its business-to-business (B2B) operations.

**Established in 2016 as a food venture, Kitchen Secret was initially discontinued due to challenges related to marketing and distribution.** Manav Kedia revived the business in 2023, driven by rising consumer interest in international flavours and the growing adoption of quick commerce in India. **The relaunch involved a brand refresh, an expanded product portfolio and the development of recipes in-house.**

**Kitchen Secret's range includes sauces inspired by Italian, Mexican and Korean cuisines.** The company operates its own manufacturing facility, with a production capacity of approximately 500 kg per day. It has sold more than one lakh jars and has a presence across over 500 Blinkit dark stores.

> **Manav Kedia, Co-Founder of Kitchen Secret, said,** “We didn't come into this with industry experience, just a love for good food and a belief that India was ready for it. Over the past three years, every day has taught us something new, and we've used each lesson to improve. Our goal is simple: to keep getting better until Kitchen Secret is the name people trust most for sauces.”

> **Radhika Jain, Co-Founder & CEO, BeyondSeed Middle East shared,** “India’s evolving consumer landscape presents an opportunity for brands that combine differentiated products with convenience and accessibility. Kitchen Secret has demonstrated the ability to build a distinct product portfolio and establish distribution across quick-commerce, retail and B2B channels while remaining bootstrapped. We are pleased to support the team as it strengthens its market presence and scales its operations. We believe the brand is well-positioned to build on its early traction and tap into the growing demand for convenient, globally inspired food products.”

**The brand sells through its official website and online platforms such as Blinkit, Zepto, and Amazon. Beyond direct-to-consumer sales, Kitchen Secret serves the hotel, restaurant, and catering (HoReCa) segment.** It also offers white-label and private-label manufacturing services to other brands, extending its presence across consumer and institutional markets.

![{Funding Alert} Banarasi Food Brand Banaraswala Secures $2 Mn in Seed Funding](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-10-15T143434.113.jpg)

Banaraswala, a food brand specialising in traditional Banarasi cuisine, has raised $2 million in seed funding from Prax Impex Private Limited. **The company plans to use the capital to establish more outlets, introduce additional menu options, and expand its franchise network across the country.**

Founded by Vibhanshu Mishra, Banaraswala focuses on regional Banarasi food, including traditional sweets, chaats, and meals. **The brand operates under the tagline “Ghat Se Ghar Tak” and incorporates elements of local food culture into its dining format through the use of kulhads, pattal, and clay-based serving accessories.**

**Banaraswala currently operates three outlets across Delhi and is preparing to enter new markets.** Its expansion plans include Banswara in Rajasthan, Sarangpur in Gujarat, and Farrukhabad and Fatehpur in Uttar Pradesh. **Customers can also order its offerings through major online food delivery platforms.**

**The company has set a target of establishing 50 outlets by March 2027 across Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Delhi-NCR and other Tier II markets.** The proposed network will comprise both company-operated stores and franchise outlets, enabling the brand to expand through different business formats.

**The newly raised funding will support the establishment of additional locations and the development of new menu offerings.** Expanding its franchise network is another priority as Banaraswala looks to enter more cities and reach a wider customer base.

**Alongside its outlet expansion, the company plans to strengthen its internal operations, build its team and improve business processes.** These measures are expected to support the management of a larger retail network as the brand moves into new markets.

**Banaraswala's expansion comes amid growing opportunities for regional food brands to establish a presence beyond their original markets.** Restaurant operators are increasingly using franchising and organised outlet formats to bring regional cuisines to consumers in different cities.

**For Banaraswala, the focus remains on expanding its physical footprint while retaining its emphasis on traditional Banarasi food.** The planned expansion to 50 outlets by March 2027 will mark a significant step in the brand's efforts to establish a wider presence across North and West India.

{Funding Alert} Confido Health Raises $12.5 Mn With Backing From Z47, Together Fund and Blume Ventures

![Indian Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/art-logo.webp)

BY - [Indian Retailer Bureau](/author/indian-retailer-bureau)  
 Sub Editor  / 1 MIN READ

[Follow Us ![Indina Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/follow.webp)](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAiEJjETmBVGGR4AF2qcS42jEMqFAgKIhCYxE5gVRhkeABdqnEuNoxD?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN%3Aen)

![{Funding Alert} Confido Health Raises $12.5 Mn With Backing From Z47, Together Fund and Blume Ventures](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-10-15T113430.304.jpg)

Healthtech startup Confido Health has raised $12.5 million in a Series A funding round led by Z47, with participation from existing investors Together Fund and Blume Ventures. **The development follows the announcement of a $10 million Series A round in September. In December 2024, the company secured $3 million in seed funding led by Together Fund.**

The company plans to deploy the latest funding to scale its artificial intelligence (AI) platform, which automates administrative processes and supports healthcare operations.

**Established in 2022 by Chetan Reddy and Vichar Shroff, Confido Health builds AI agents to manage routine healthcare tasks, including appointment bookings, insurance verification, and care coordination.** Its technology connects with existing healthcare systems through a no-code deployment process, which the company claims takes less than five minutes to complete.

**Confido Health's platform integrates with over 50 systems, covering electronic health records, practice management software, telephone systems, billing platforms and fax systems.** The company said healthcare providers can adopt its solutions without replacing their existing technology infrastructure.

**The startup currently serves around 3,200 healthcare providers across more than 1,500 care sites in 27 states, with independent practice groups forming a significant part of its network.** According to the company, one in every 50 patients can now reach their healthcare providers through its AI agents.

**The platform collects patient information, referral details, and payer requirements during the intake process.** It then uses these details to coordinate follow-up activities, including patient outreach and scheduling. **Confido Health said a single interaction can initiate several workflows, such as referral management, appointment booking, prescription refills, and payment processing.**

**The company reported 15-fold growth since its previous funding round.** It also stated that its AI agents have achieved handle rates of more than 95 percent across key end-to-end administrative workflows. **Additionally, Confido Health claims that its platform can provide operational capacity equivalent to three to five full-time employees on average within three months of implementation.**

**Confido Health is targeting multiple medical specialties, including ophthalmology and optometry, physical therapy, dental care, primary care, and community care.** Its focus is on automating administrative responsibilities and helping healthcare providers manage routine operations through AI-based systems.
