Design-led lifestyle tech brand DailyObjects has appointed Zeenah Vilcassim as its Global Chief Marketing Officer (CMO), as the company strengthens its leadership team to support its international growth plans.

**With more than 17 years of experience across markets including the US, Europe, the Middle East, China, and India, Vilcassim brings expertise in brand building, consumer business growth, and market expansion.**

In her new role, she will oversee DailyObjects’ global brand and marketing strategy, helping the company build on its presence in India while accelerating its ambitions in international markets.

**Before joining DailyObjects, Vilcassim led marketing for Nothing in India.** She also served as CEO of Zomato Live, now known as District by Zomato, where she was responsible for building the business from the ground up. > **Pankaj Garg, Co-Founder and CEO, DailyObjects said**, *"DailyObjects is entering its next chapter. We want to build a brand that means something to people, wherever they are. > **Zeenah Vilcassim, Global Chief Marketing Officer, DailyObjects shared,** *"DailyObjects has already built the foundations of a truly distinctive lifestyle brand: a strong understanding of contemporary consumers and a clear point of view on how design fits into their daily lives. Pankaj and Saurav's ambition to take this India-born brand to the world is something DailyObjects is strongly poised to achieve, with both its local relevance and international appeal. I look forward to joining them on the next stage of this journey, making DailyObjects a brand that is meaningful to consumers' daily lives wherever it goes."*

**The appointment comes at a time when DailyObjects is expanding its global footprint and strengthening its design-focused product portfolio.** The company, which offers technology accessories, carry solutions, workspace essentials, and lifestyle products, recently showcased its offerings at IFA Berlin 2026, marking its first international exhibition and an important step toward building partnerships with global retailers and distributors.

Preventive pain care startup betterhood has secured Rs 11.5 crore in a seed funding round led by Sauce, with participation from existing investor Kairon Capital.

**Earlier this year, the Bengaluru-based company had raised Rs 5 crore in the same funding round led by Kairon Capital.** The round also saw participation from Yogesh Kabra, Rishubh Satiya, Rohit Chawla, Sifat Khurana, and Shayamal Vallabhjee.

**The newly raised capital will be utilized to strengthen its product offerings, widen its presence across quick commerce and modern retail channels, and expand its content initiatives and physiotherapist network.**

Established in October 2024 by Vikram Kadam and Neha Zade, **betterhood focuses on preventive pain care solutions designed to address early symptoms of back, neck, and joint discomfort.**

**The brand offers a range of products including posture and ergonomic supports, orthotic soft goods such as back, knee, ankle, and wrist supports, as well as pain relief and recovery solutions.**

**The company said these product categories collectively account for an estimated Rs 20,000 crore market in India and continue to grow at a low- to mid-teen rate.**

As part of its ecosystem approach, betterhood has developed Physio Circle, a nationwide community dedicated to creating awareness around posture, movement, pain prevention, and recovery. The network currently includes more than 7,000 physiotherapists.

**The company has also introduced The Physio Edge, a certification program aimed at helping early-career physiotherapists bridge the gap between academic education and practical clinical experience.**

Since launching operations, **betterhood claims to have served more than 2 lakh customers and created over 1,500 educational content pieces across digital platforms focused on posture, movement, pain prevention, and recovery.**

**The preventive pain management segment has witnessed increased investor interest in recent years.** Nivaan Care raised $7 million to expand its non-surgical chronic pain management clinics, while Litemed’s CURAPOD secured Rs 20 crore in a pre-Series A funding round to scale its photobiomodulation-based wearable pain management technology. **Heatronics also raised Rs 1.8 crore to strengthen its preventive pain management and heat therapy device portfolio.**

**In 2025, Zanskar secured Rs 2.8 crore to broaden its pain care product range and invest in research and development for chronic pain and recovery solutions.** Meanwhile, Stance Health raised $1 million to advance its technology-driven musculoskeletal care platform, which integrates diagnosis, physiotherapy, and recovery programs.

Lifestyle and tech accessories brand DailyObjects is reportedly in the final stages of securing a funding round worth approximately Rs 350 crore, with Xponentia Capital and Anicut Capital’s growth equity fund expected to lead the investment. **The transaction could value the Gurugram-based company at around Rs 1,000 crore.**

**The proposed round is expected to include a mix of primary and secondary share sales.** The fresh capital will likely be used to broaden DailyObjects’ product offerings, strengthen its distribution network, and support efforts to reach a larger customer base.

Founded in 2012 by Pankaj Garg and Saurav Adlakha, DailyObjects began as a design-led accessories brand focused on blending technology, utility, and aesthetics. Over the years, the company has expanded beyond smartphone accessories to build a wider portfolio that includes phone cases, laptop sleeves, smartwatch accessories, charging products, tech gadgets, organizers, bags, wallets, pouches, and workplace essentials.

**The brand has also increased its offline retail presence through exclusive stores, airport outlets, and partnerships with Apple Premium Retail locations.** According to reports, DailyObjects is now available across more than 250 retail locations spanning over 85 cities, including major metropolitan markets and airport retail hubs.

**The company has been investing in both product expansion and offline growth as it works toward scaling revenue and improving profitability.** Earlier this year, founder Pankaj Garg told CNBC-TV18 that DailyObjects expected to close FY26 with net revenue between Rs 215 crore and Rs 220 crore, while targeting revenue of Rs 400 crore in the current financial year. The anticipated growth is being driven by an expanding retail footprint and a broader product portfolio.

The upcoming funding round follows previous investments from firms including Seedfund, Unilazer Ventures, Roots Ventures, 360 One, and Trifecta Capital Advisors. **The company has raised approximately $14.5 million in funding to date.**

**DailyObjects was exploring a fundraise of around Rs 300 crore through a combination of primary and secondary transactions, with Xponentia Capital expected to lead the round.** The latest developments suggest that the size of the transaction has increased to approximately Rs 350 crore, with the inclusion of Anicut Capital’s growth equity fund.

Delhi-based high-protein frozen food brand Protein Pantry has secured Rs 9 crore in a seed funding round led by Sharrp Ventures, with participation from Peercheque, Consumer Collective by Atrium, and Indian Silicon Valley Capital. **The round also saw backing from angel investors including Varun Alagh, Rishubh Satiya, Avnish Anand, Arush Chopra, Saurabh Munjal, Signal Ventures, and others.**

**The newly raised capital will be used to strengthen its manufacturing capabilities, scale production, and support ongoing investments in research and development as well as supply chain operations.**

**Founded in November last year by Disha Bhattacharya and Prashanth Bhushan, Protein Pantry operates in the clean-label frozen food segment, offering high-protein, ready-to-cook products designed for Indian households.** The company said its products are made using kitchen-shelf ingredients and do not contain refined flour, preservatives, or palm oil. The brand follows a 1:10 protein-to-calorie ratio across its portfolio and manufactures all products in-house.

**Protein Pantry has expanded its direct-to-consumer presence across Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Jaipur.** The brand is also available on quick commerce platforms including Blinkit, FirstClub, and Flipkart Minutes in Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad.

The company stated that it has served more than 30,000 households so far and recorded a strong repeat purchase rate. **It is planning to extend its quick commerce presence to Pune, Kolkata, Lucknow, Chandigarh, Ludhiana, and Chennai by the end of the year.**

**The brand is focused on addressing growing demand for protein-rich food options beyond traditional supplements and snack products.** Its current portfolio includes baked soya chaap, kebabs, cutlets, and falafels, all produced without refined flour, preservatives, or palm oil. Protein Pantry also develops its marinades, sauces, and chaap base at its own manufacturing facility.

**Looking ahead, the company plans to introduce new product formats and expand its protein-focused portfolio over the next 12 to 24 months.** It aims to strengthen its footprint across major Indian cities through both direct-to-consumer and quick commerce channels.

Electric commercial mobility startup Drivn has secured Rs 45 crore (approximately $4.7 million) in a seed funding round led by Avaana Capital, strengthening its efforts to build an integrated electric mobility platform for commercial transportation in India.

**The funding comes several months after the company announced an $80 million capital commitment from Japanese financial services firm Nomura in February 2026.** While that commitment was made at the group level, the latest investment has been raised by Drivn’s Indian operating entity. The company’s parent holding firm is headquartered in Singapore.

**The board of Drivn’s Indian entity approved the issuance of 33,98,792 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at a price of Rs 132.40 per share.** Avaana Capital participated as the sole investor in the funding round, contributing the entire Rs 45 crore.

**The company plans to utilize the newly raised capital to support business expansion, operational requirements, and other general corporate purposes.**

**Founded in 2025 by Manav Bansal and Alpna Jain, Gurugram-based Drivn is focused on developing a full-stack electric mobility ecosystem for large commercial vehicles.** The startup operates in the electric transportation segment by owning and leasing electric intercity buses and heavy-duty trucks, while also providing fleet management and operational services to commercial fleet operators.

**Beyond vehicle deployment, Drivn offers charging infrastructure solutions and battery lifecycle management services, aiming to support businesses transitioning from conventional fleets to electric mobility.**

**Following the latest investment, Drivn Transition PTE. LTD, the Singapore-based parent company, continues to hold a majority stake of 88.75 percent in the Indian business.** Avaana Capital now owns 7.22 percent, while co-founder and Chief Executive Officer Manav Bansal holds 4.03 percent.

**Despite securing funding and attracting strategic backing, the Indian entity remained at a pre-revenue stage during FY26.** Regulatory filings show that the company reported a loss of Rs 1.96 crore during the financial year as it continued to invest in building its operations and platform capabilities.

**The latest funding underscores growing investor interest in the commercial electric vehicle ecosystem, particularly in areas such as fleet electrification, charging infrastructure, and integrated mobility services.**

# IIT Alumni & Former P&G Colleagues Scale Healthy Snack Brand Open Secret to Rs 87 Cr Revenue in FY25; Losses Shrink to Rs 7 Cr

Open Secret reported Rs 87 Cr revenue in FY25, up 62% YoY, while losses shrank 72% to Rs 7.1 Cr, as the healthy snack brand improved efficiency and moved closer to breakeven.

Open Secret to Rs 87 Cr Revenue in FY25; Losses Shrink to Rs 7 Cr

Healthy snack brand Open Secret reported a 62% increase in revenue to Rs 87.25 crore in FY25, up from Rs 54 crore in FY24, according to its consolidated financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Revenue from product sales stood at Rs 85.5 crore in FY25, rising from Rs 53.5 crore in FY24. The company also recorded Rs 1.75 crore in other income during the fiscal year.

On the expenditure front, total expenses grew by 18% to Rs 93.6 crore in FY25, compared to Rs 79.1 crore in FY24. The largest cost component, cost of goods sold, increased by 55% to Rs 42.8 crore from Rs 27.6 crore in the previous year.

Employee benefit expenses declined by 41% to Rs 6 crore in FY25, down from Rs 10.2 crore in FY24. Meanwhile, marketing expenses surged by 42% to Rs 29 crore, up from Rs 20.5 crore a year earlier.

![TBI Logo](https://static-cdn.publive.online/english-betterindia/media/media_files/2025/10/06/gda-logo-light-2-2025-10-06-15-39-59.png)

Despite rising expenses, the company significantly reduced its net loss by 72% to Rs 7.1 crore in FY25, compared to Rs 25 crore in FY24. On a unit economics basis, Open Secret spent Rs 1.09 to earn every rupee in FY25, improving from Rs 1.48 in FY24, indicating a clear move toward breakeven.

## About Open Secret

Open Secret (legal name: Immaculatebites Private Limited) is a Mumbai-based health food brand founded in 2019 by Ahana Gautam and Udit Kejriwal, who first met while working at Procter & Gamble (P&G). Both founders come from strong academic backgrounds. Ahana is an alumna of IIT Bombay and Harvard Business School, while Udit studied at IIT Kharagpur and IIM Ahmedabad.

The company aims to “un-junk” Indian snacking by offering products free from palm oil, maida, and artificial preservatives. It focuses on delivering a “better-for-you” snacking experience, primarily targeting families and children.

Its key product categories include cookies and biscuits, breakfast foods, namkeen, protein and nutrition products, as well as dry fruits and seeds.

Initially launched in Mumbai, the brand has expanded to a pan-India presence through e-commerce platforms such as Amazon, Flipkart, and BigBasket, along with quick-commerce platforms like Blinkit and Zepto.

To date, Open Secret has raised approximately $14.2 million (around Rs 118 crore). Its latest major funding round, a Series B, saw the company raise $9.98 million in June 2022, led by Ananta Capital. Earlier, it secured Rs 18 crore (around $2.5 million) in its Series A round in July 2021, led by Sixth Sense Ventures.

# How Beyond Snack has Grown its Business Post Shark Tank

![Indian Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/art-logo.webp)
![IndianRetailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/brandlicense/themes/custom/menshealth/images/vicon.webp)
![IR](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/fshare.webp)
![IR](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/flink.webp)

![Indian Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/follow.webp)
![How Beyond Snack has Grown its Business Post Shark Tank](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2023-01/3%20%284%29%20%281%29.jpg "How Beyond Snack has Grown its Business Post Shark Tank")

Beyond Snacks is a brand that offers authentic banana chips in a variety of flavors. The brand thus offers products using premium quality raw materials while maintaining hygiene, claiming to offer the best ever banana chips to taste. Thus, Beyond Snack with its product portfolio wants to make authentic premium quality banana chips available across the country. Today, the brand is backed by sharks post its appearance on Shark Tank India, Season 1, and has turned its business around.

With an aim to start his own business, Manas Madhu, Co-Founder, Beyond Snack delved into the subject of the food business, post coming across an article. “The more I learned, the more I became interested in this subject. Finally made the decision to relocate to Kerala and take a new job. During the week, I worked for another company, and on weekends, I traveled to meet people who were directly or indirectly involved with food,” said Manas.

**The Inception**

Madhu initially presented a vegetable-based mock meat product, but it was a failed experiment. However, one bad bag of chips made him realize the absence of an organized banana chip market in India.

“The banana chips market is comparatively undeveloped with respect to the enormous market for potato chips. I made the decision to give it a try, and over the course of two months, I visited 42 chip manufacturers and learned one important lesson. None of the chip manufacturers adhere to any hygiene or best cooking practices,” said Manas Madhu.

He further added, ***“I saw an opportunity and decided to get to work on this concept. With the help of friends who work for different food businesses, I started attempting to establish standards and procedures for the production of banana chips. I quit my job and decided to devote all of my time to this endeavor. The product was finally released in the market in January 2020.”***

Beyond Snack began with a trade show, which validated the product's market acceptance, thus allowing the brand to introduce its product in major cities. However, owing to the Covid lockdown, it shifted its emphasis to the online delivery platform.

**Currently, Beyond Snack products are accessible on all e-commerce platforms, having launched its products on retail platforms a year ago. The brand has a strong presence in Maharashtra and in major metropolitan areas such as Bangalore, Chennai, Hyderabad, and Delhi, among others.**

![How Beyond Snack Has Grown its Business post Shark Tank](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/inline-images/3%20%285%29%20%281%29.jpg)

![How Beyond Snack Has Grown its Business post Shark Tank](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/inline-images/3%20%285%29%20%281%29.jpg)

**The Ever-Growing Snack Market**

Despite the fact that numerous brands have introduced banana chips, according to the co-founder there was barely any distinction between them and locally produced banana chips.

The primary issue in this field has been innovation, studies, and research. There was no consistency in the overall experience provided by banana chips with less emphasis on hygiene and manufacturing standards.

Beyond snack, began identifying and resolving these issues, with its priority being to provide customers with a healthy, satisfying experience. ***“Our chips are thinner, crisper, lighter, tastier, and healthier than other brands,”*** added Madhu.

The brand thus obtains bananas from farmers in Kerala and other southern Indian states based on seasonal availability, which is then processed in its Kochi factory without human intervention and is further sold through e-commerce platforms, retail stores, and supermarkets.

Madhu further added, ***“We have implemented standardization at all stages of the cooking process. When compared to a conventional banana chip maker, this reduces the cooking time of sliced bananas by one-tenth. Compared to regular banana chips, this has a 20 percent fat reduction and less oil exposure.”***

Bananas harvested directly from the plantain tree are transformed into chips within twenty-four hours, adding an additional dimension of farm freshness to Beyond Snack offerings, its other characteristics include less fat, lighter for the stomach, and consistently crisp thin slices.

**Options Galore**

Beyond Snack's original portfolio of banana chips included four varieties- Original salted, Peri Peri, Sour cream onion parsley, and Salt Black pepper. The brand has recently introduced two additional flavors including Desi Masala and Hot Sweet Chilli. **In the upcoming months, it plans to introduce 20 additional variants, many of which will feature significant innovations.**

Although the brand's current emphasis is on Banana chips, they have plans to expand into additional categories. The Indian snack market remains extremely fragmented. The snack industry offers many opportunities for organized play. In the coming years, Beyond Snack aims to develop its expertise in other categories.

**Technology and Beyond Snack**

With its belief that the supply chain is the genesis of technological innovations. For its banana chips, the brand uses a particular variety called Nendran.

Additionally, it looks into how to make the experience consistent and as a result, has altered the entire manufacturing process.

The Banana chips are typically made in a kadai and are cooked for up to 20 minutes. However, Beyond Snack has installed a system that guarantees a stable and controlled environment for cooking, providing greater control over the cooking procedure.

Additionally, it has acquired innovations in different seasoning mixes and packaging.  
Moreover, the brand aims to bring in more technological innovations, reinstating the same, Manas Madhu commented, “We believe that the foundation of business excellence is a mindset of continuous improvement. Therein lays the cornerstone of our organization. Our team of innovators is currently putting the finishing touches on a number of significant new banana chip innovations that will hit the market this year.”

![How Beyond Snack Has Grown its Business post Shark Tank](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/inline-images/3%20%286%29%20%281%29.jpg)

![How Beyond Snack Has Grown its Business post Shark Tank](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/inline-images/3%20%286%29%20%281%29.jpg)

**Growth Post Shark Tank**

Beyond Snack received investment from Aman Gupta, Co-Founder-CMO of boAt, and Ashneer Grover, Co-Founder, BharatPe. While both sharks bring unique skills and capabilities to the table, the co-founder stated that Aman excels at branding and marketing and Ashneer's strength lies in organizational development and growth.

“Both skills are extremely complementary. Ashneer taught us about lightning-fast execution and strategies for bringing about hyper-growth, while Aman taught us about different layers of storytelling in branding and marketing. Our approach to the game was fundamentally altered by the Sharks' knowledge and experience,” added Madhu.

Moreover, owing to its team’s aggressive and tireless approach to providing its customers throughout India with excellent banana chips, every year, Beyond Snack is able to grow six-fold. ***“The year 2023 will be crucial, as we anticipate double-digit growth over the previous year,”*** stated Madhu.

**The brand has raised over Rs 5.5 crore from angel investors and micro-venture capitalists.**

**Retail and Marketing**

***“We see ourselves as a purely FMCG company. Retail/GT is still close to our hearts. Therefore, we have a pro-retail strategy,”*** said Manas.

The brand aims to launch operations in India's major cities within the upcoming 12 months. In November 2022, it released its first marketing campaign, ‘*24Carat Taste*’, reflecting the strong alignment between its story and its core mission of providing customers with an experience of the highest caliber.

**At the moment, the brand’s marketing is more heavily skewed toward digital. Its direct-to-consumer presence is primarily through marketplaces such as Amazon and Flipkart and is also present on other online platforms, including Big Basket, Swiggy, Blinkit, Zepto, and others.**

**Future Plans**

From obtaining bananas from farmers directly, the brand produces in Kerala and supplies from there. Moreover, currently, the brand has distributors in Maharashtra's major cities, including Mumbai, Pune, Nashik, Nagpur, Amaravati, Aurangabad, etc.

In Maharashtra, Beyond Snack has a large distribution network and will be expanding its distribution presence to other states this year as well. As a result, more customers will have access to banana chips of higher quality, the current plan however is to expand into 23 additional cities within this year. The brand is already developing more flavor options for its customers.

“In the next five years, Beyond Snack will be a well-known national brand with a strong presence in additional food and beverage categories. Our core focus will remain on providing our customers with a gold-standard experience,” concluded Manas Madhu.

![From Everyday Feeding to Science-Led Nutrition: How Drools Is Tapping India's Evolving Pet Food Market](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/2%20%282%29.jpg)

India's pet food market is witnessing a shift as pet ownership grows and consumers increasingly treat pets as family members. What was once largely a functional purchase centred on feeding is gradually evolving into a more considered category, with pet parents paying closer attention to ingredients, nutritional balance, product formats and health benefits. For organised pet food companies, this changing mindset is creating opportunities across premium nutrition, wet food, fresh food, functional products and digital commerce.

For Drools Pet Food, the transformation of consumer behaviour is opening up new avenues for growth. Over the past two to three years, the company has expanded its international presence, strengthened its premium portfolio and invested in emerging product categories to address the changing expectations of pet parents.

According to Rakhi Rana, COO, Drools Pet Food Pvt Ltd, the company's business has recorded a three-year CAGR of approximately 75%, reflecting the momentum behind its expansion strategy and the growing demand for packaged pet nutrition.

"The way pet parents approach nutrition is changing. They are becoming more informed and deliberate about what goes into their pets' food. They want to understand ingredients, preparation methods and nutritional balance, while increasingly looking for food that feels closer to a home-cooked meal. At the same time, packaged pet food has become part of the regular household shopping basket, making convenience, affordability, consistency and trust important purchasing considerations," says Rana.

##### **The Shift Towards Premium and Fresh Nutrition**

India's expanding pet population is providing a strong foundation for the organised pet food industry. The country's pet population increased from 28.4 million in 2020 to 39.2 million in 2025, indicating a growing consumer base for pet-care products. According to IMARC Group, India's pet food market was valued at approximately USD 2.4 billion in 2024 and is projected to reach USD 4.6 billion by 2033, growing at a CAGR of 7.2% between 2025 and 2033.

As the category develops, consumers are moving beyond basic feeding requirements towards products that offer specific nutritional benefits. This is particularly visible in the growing interest in wet food and fresh-style formats, which combine recognisable ingredients, higher moisture content and ready-to-serve convenience.

Drools is addressing this shift through its Fresh Food range, featuring meat-rich recipes formulated without corn, wheat, soy or preservatives. The portfolio currently includes four variants: Real Chicken & Veggies, Real Chicken & Pumpkin, Real Chicken and Turkey, and Real Chicken Biryani.

The company has also opted for Tetra Recart packaging, allowing the products to offer home-style meals with complete and balanced nutrition while maintaining freshness and flavour without requiring refrigeration before opening.

"Consumers are increasingly looking for food formats that offer both nutritional value and convenience. Our Fresh Food range responds to this demand by bringing together recognisable ingredients, balanced nutrition and easy-to-serve packaging. We want to make home-style meals a convenient part of everyday feeding routines," Rana explains.

The company's product development strategy also extends to vegetarian offerings. Its 100% Veg Gravy is a moist, plant-derived mealtime option for dogs, catering to households seeking alternatives to meat-based products. Drools is further expanding its wet-food portfolio with bone broth and soups, alongside functional treats for dogs and cats.

##### **Premiumisation Creates New Growth Opportunities**

Premiumisation is emerging as another important growth driver for the company. Drools' premium dog food portfolio includes Focus, Canine Creek and Grain Zero, supported by breeder and veterinarian partnerships.

While premium pet food continues to represent a relatively low-volume, high-margin segment, the company sees considerable potential in educating consumers about the nutritional benefits of value-added products.

The broader portfolio spans dry and wet food for dogs and cats, treats, veterinary prescription diets, supplements and pharmaceutical products. Its formulations include grain-free, single-grain and high-meat recipes, reflecting a focus on different nutritional requirements.

For Drools, the opportunity lies not just in introducing premium products but also in building consumer understanding around the role of nutrition in pet health.

"Premiumisation is steadily gaining momentum, but consumer education remains important. Through our premium portfolio, veterinarian relationships and emerging categories such as Fresh Food and Bone Broth, we aim to communicate the nutritional benefits of value-added products and encourage their long-term adoption," says Rana.

##### **Digital Commerce Reshapes Distribution**

The changing purchase behaviour of pet parents is also influencing the company's distribution strategy. Drools currently reaches more than 2,000 cities through nearly 50,000 retail touchpoints, while its e-commerce presence provides product accessibility across 100% of serviceable PIN codes in India.

However, digital commerce is increasingly becoming a significant part of its business model. E-commerce accounts for nearly 40% of the company's overall Indian business, while general trade and modern trade each contribute less than 10%.

Quick commerce is emerging as another important growth channel, registering triple-digit year-on-year growth.

The shift reflects the growing preference for convenience-led shopping among younger pet parents, who are increasingly discovering and purchasing new products through digital platforms. Categories such as Cat Mousse, Fresh Food for Dogs and treats for dogs and cats are witnessing accelerated growth across these channels.

As digital commerce gains momentum, the company is looking to use these platforms not only to improve accessibility but also to introduce consumers to newer formats and encourage product experimentation.

##### **International Markets: A New Growth Engine**

While India remains Drools' primary market, international expansion is becoming an increasingly important part of its long-term strategy. Exports currently contribute less than 5% to the company's overall business, but the company is aggressively pursuing triple-digit export growth in FY27.

The strategy is centred on three distinct regions, the GCC, Southeast Asia and Africa, each presenting different consumer preferences and category opportunities.

In the GCC, Drools has established a presence across the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Bahrain, Qatar and Kuwait. The UAE and Saudi Arabia are its key growth markets, supported by rising demand for premium, health-led pet nutrition. The company also operates through its own entity and a dedicated team in Dubai to manage regional operations.

The region is predominantly cat-food-led, with cats accounting for approximately 70% of the pet-care category. The Indian diaspora has helped build familiarity with the brand, while Indian-manufactured pet products are also gaining acceptance among local consumers.

Southeast Asia presents another opportunity, particularly through the growth of digital consumers and e-commerce. Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, the Philippines and Vietnam are important markets for the company. Its strategy in the region focuses on premium cat food, prescription diets, veterinary relationships and wider distribution through supermarkets and modern trade.

Africa, meanwhile, represents a more volume-driven opportunity. Markets such as Ghana, Nigeria and Tanzania are seeing the expansion of pet shops, veterinary clinics, supermarkets and organised retail channels. Drools is working with breeders and pet shops to build awareness around packaged pet nutrition, with affordability and accessibility remaining key priorities.

"The international opportunity is not a one-size-fits-all proposition. The GCC is driven by demand for premium nutrition, Southeast Asia offers opportunities through digital commerce and premium cat food, while Africa is a more volume-led market where affordability and distribution are critical. We are building our approach around the specific needs of pet parents in each region," says Rana.

The company's export growth strategy is being supported by its cat food portfolio. Newer offerings, including Cat Mousse and Cat Gravy Chunks, are expected to strengthen its position in international markets and accelerate growth.

##### **Investing in Innovation and Scientific Credibility**

Product innovation remains central to Drools' strategy as it looks to differentiate itself in an increasingly competitive category. Alongside expanding its product formats, the company is continuously augmenting its manufacturing facilities and developing an R&D centre in Rajnandgaon, Chhattisgarh.

Its participation in the 51st World Small Animal Veterinary Association (WSAVA) World Congress in Warsaw marked another step in its international engagement. As the first Indian pet-care brand to exhibit at the Congress, Drools showcased its Drools, Vet Pro and Drools Fresh Food portfolios to the global veterinary community.

The company also introduced three specialised feline prescription diets under its expanded Vet Pro range: Cat Obesity, Gastrointestinal for Cats and Cat Urocare. These products are designed to address specific health requirements under veterinary guidance.

The focus on science-led nutrition is also reflected in the company's efforts to develop newer categories that appeal to younger consumers, including Gen Z and the emerging Gen Alpha cohort.

For Drools, innovation is therefore extending beyond traditional dry kibble to include wet food, fresh meals, bone broth, soups, functional treats and specialised nutrition.

##### **Building the Next Phase of Growth**

Over the next three to five years, Drools' priorities will centre on strengthening consumer trust, expanding product accessibility and developing emerging categories. The company intends to use consumer feedback and repeat purchases to guide the expansion of its Fresh Food range, while continuing to build its vegetarian and meat-based wet-food offerings.

Veterinarian partnerships and scientific credibility will remain important pillars of its growth strategy, particularly as consumers become more conscious of the relationship between nutrition and pet health.

With India continuing to anchor its business and exports emerging as a long-term growth opportunity, Drools is positioning itself across multiple segments of the evolving pet food market.

As Rana puts it, the company's focus is on making science-led nutrition and meaningful innovation accessible to more pet parents. The opportunity ahead will depend not just on expanding distribution or introducing new products, but on building consumer confidence in packaged pet nutrition as an everyday part of responsible pet care.

![RESET Plans Retail Expansion across Tier II markets, Diversifies Beyond Pain Relief Into New Wellness Categories](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/seoo%20imagee1%20%2829%29.jpg)

Launched in July 2021, RESET entered the Indian wellness market with a proposition that brought together pharmaceutical formulation science and natural, Ayurveda-rooted ingredients. Backed by Venus Remedies, a research-driven pharmaceutical company with over 35 years of experience in critical care and antimicrobial research, the brand was developed at the Natural Products Research Lab of Venus Medicine Research Centre (VMRC), the company's R&D division.

The idea behind RESET emerged from a gap its founders identified in the Indian pain management market. Indian consumers largely approached pain relief reactively, seeking solutions only when discomfort began affecting their daily lives. The available choices were also divided between conventional painkillers and traditional remedies that often lacked scientific validation.

"We saw an opportunity to bridge that gap by bringing the rigour of pharmaceutical formulation science to natural, Ayurveda-rooted ingredients. Our topical range uses proprietary nanotechnology that helps actives penetrate nearly five times faster than conventional preparations, which is what allows a natural formulation to perform at a clinically meaningful level," shared Saransh Chaudhary, Founder, RESET and CEO, VMRC.

What began as a pain relief business gradually evolved into a broader wellness proposition as consumer insights revealed demand for products that addressed everyday well-being rather than occasional discomfort.

"We began with pain relief, but consumer insight quickly made it evident that people were looking for far more than episodic relief. They wanted a partner in their everyday well-being. That insight shaped RESET's evolution from a pain management brand into a holistic wellness brand, and it is why RESET is built around three ideas: Relief, Revive and Restore," he said.

Today, this philosophy guides the brand's product development and retail approach, with a portfolio spanning pain relief, recovery, sleep, gut health and daily nutrition.

## Building an Omnichannel Distribution Network

RESET's retail footoprint comprises e-commerce marketplaces, its direct-to-consumer (D2C) platform, quick commerce, modern retail and specialised wellness spaces. In online retail, Amazon is currently its leading marketplace, while its own website serves as a direct channel for consumer engagement and repeat purchases. The brand is also available on Blinkit, allowing consumers to access its products through quick commerce.

Offline, RESET has established a presence through modern retail partners, including Broadway, across cities such as Delhi, Pune and Hyderabad. It is also present on Smytten across Noida, Ahmedabad and Indore. Beyond conventional retail, the brand is tapping boutique wellness centres, Pilates studios and fitness centres, where its pain relief and recovery products find relevant consumers.

"Our distribution strategy is built on one principle: meet the consumer at the moment the need arises. RESET operates across a set of complementary channels, each doing a distinct job," Chaudhary said.

Explaining the rationale behind its channel mix, he said the objective is to create an ecosystem where product discovery, trial and repeat purchases reinforce one another.

"Our channel choices have been deliberate rather than opportunistic. The intent has been to build an ecosystem in which discovery, trial and repeat purchase reinforce one another, so that every channel earns its place and strengthens the next," he added.

The brand's current revenue mix reflects the importance of online marketplaces, with Amazon leading on volume. However, its D2C platform also contributes a meaningful share, giving the company an opportunity to build stronger consumer relationships and understand purchasing behaviour.

"Marketplaces, with Amazon in particular, currently lead on volume, while our own platform contributes a materially larger share than is typical for a brand at this stage, and that is the number we watch most closely," Chaudhary said.

He added that the contribution from its own platform indicates that consumers are increasingly willing to engage directly with the brand, supporting retention and long-term customer value.

## Expanding Beyond Pain Relief

RESET currently has around 15 products across four categories: Pain Relief, Wellness, Vitals and Yoga. While pain relief remains its core category, the brand is building its portfolio around recovery, preventive wellness and everyday nutrition.

Its leading pain relief products include Ultra Potent Gel, Pain Relief Roll-On Emulsion, Deep Penetrating Spray and Instant Ease Tablets. These address muscular discomfort and everyday aches associated with modern, sedentary lifestyles.

Another important product in its portfolio is Stretch Easy Oil, a research-backed Abhyanga formulation featuring chamomile, lemongrass, eucalyptus and camphor. Positioned within its Yoga portfolio, the product is used before or after yoga sessions to ease stiffness and support mobility.

"Along with the Emulsion, it records our highest repeat purchase rates, which tells us that recovery, and not only relief, is where the deeper relationship with a consumer is built," Chaudhary said.

In its Wellness and Vitals categories, Herbal Detox Candy has emerged as one of the fastest-growing products. The formulation combines five Ayurvedic herbs: Kalmegh, Manjishta, Guduchi, Punarnava and Daru Haldi extracts.

The brand is also witnessing adoption of Marine Collagen Peptides and its gummies range, which includes Biotin and Ashwagandha with Melatonin. These products reflect growing consumer interest in preventive wellness, beauty-from-within solutions and daily-care formats.

"Across categories, the common thread is formulation integrity: products that consumers can integrate into their routines with confidence," he said.

## Entering Everyday Skin and Wound Care

The next phase of RESET's product expansion will take the brand into everyday skin and wound care. The company sees an opportunity in a category where it believes consumers need more credible, science-led solutions.

The upcoming products have been developed in-house using the company's proprietary patented formulations, allowing RESET to extend its research-led approach into another everyday health category.

"This is a natural extension of our philosophy. Wherever there is an everyday health need that remains underserved by credible, science-led solutions, there is a role for RESET," Chaudhary expressed.

The planned expansion also signals the brand's intention to move beyond its initial positioning as a pain management player and establish a wider presence in the preventive wellness market.

## Strengthening Retail Reach Across Metros and Tier II Markets

Over the next two to three years, RESET plans to strengthen its retail presence by deepening distribution in established markets while expanding into newer geographies. The brand is already receiving orders from across the country, with consumption particularly strong in Mumbai, Bengaluru and Delhi NCR. It is also witnessing encouraging traction in Tier II cities, including Jaipur, Jodhpur, Bhubaneswar, Jamshedpur and Panchkula.

This demand is shaping its expansion priorities, particularly as preventive wellness products gain traction beyond metropolitan markets.

"Preventive wellness is no longer a metro conversation, and that shapes how we plan distribution. Our approach is to go deeper in the markets where demand is already proven, while steadily widening our reach across the rest of the country in a planned manner," Chaudhary said.

In established markets, the company will focus on strengthening product availability through modern retail, expanding partnerships with fitness and wellness spaces, and building a presence at airports. The latter is an opportunity to reach travelling consumers who may be looking for products addressing fatigue, discomfort and recovery.

"Adding geographies is the more straightforward part of retail. Building density in markets where demand is already validated is what creates a durable business, and we are pursuing both in sequence rather than trading one against the other," he added.

## Making Everyday Wellness a Household Habit

For RESET, long-term growth is closely linked to changing how Indian consumers approach health and wellness. Rather than limiting product consumption to occasions when discomfort becomes disruptive, the brand wants to encourage consumers to incorporate preventive wellness into their everyday routines.

Its 'Dose of Good' philosophy brings together pharmaceutical science and natural healing, with the objective of developing products that deliver benefits while remaining suitable for regular use.

"Our long-term vision is to shift the way India approaches everyday health, from a model that is largely reactive to one that is preventive and habitual. Today, most consumers engage with pain relief or wellness products only when discomfort becomes impossible to ignore. We want RESET to be part of the routine long before that point," Chaudhary concluded.

As the brand expands its categories, distribution network and consumer touchpoints, its larger ambition is to build a wellness business rooted in research, formulation integrity and everyday relevance.

"If, over the next decade, RESET becomes synonymous with everyday well-being in Indian households, and a reference point for how natural wellness can be both credible and effective, we will have achieved what we set out to do," he said.

![Redefining Mall Retail: Kamakshi Mantri on Changing Consumer Expectations](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/WhatsApp%20Image%202026-10-30%20at%206.58.26%20PM.jpg)

The retail landscape in India is undergoing a significant transformation. As digital-first brands increasingly explore physical retail, shopping centres are evolving beyond traditional destinations for buying products. Consumers today seek experiences, convenience, engagement, and a sense of connection with the brands they interact with. For retailers and mall developers alike, understanding these changing expectations is becoming central to building successful retail businesses.

*In an interaction with Retailer Media, Kamakshi Mantri, Chief Strategy Officer, Mantri Group, discusses the nuances of transitioning from online to offline retail, the importance of festive shopping in India, and the growing role of food and beverage (F&B) spaces in shaping the modern mall experience.*

## **D2C Brands: Why Offline Retail Requires a Different Mindset**

For direct-to-consumer (D2C) brands that have built their businesses online, entering physical retail is an exciting opportunity. However, the transition requires more than simply replicating an online store in a physical environment. It calls for a fundamental shift in how brands understand consumer behaviour and the shopping journey.

According to Mantri, one of the most common mistakes D2C brands make when opening their first physical store is underestimating the importance of store design and the psychology behind it.

**“A store is not just a website with four walls. It's so much more to it,” she emphasized.**

Unlike online shopping, where consumers largely interact with products through images, descriptions and digital interfaces, an offline store engages multiple senses. Everything, from the lighting and layout to the fragrance, mirrors, product placement and overall ambience, influences the customer's perception and purchasing decisions.

“When a customer walks in, what are the first items that greet them? How does the lighting look? How does the mirror make them feel when they try on their clothes? What is the quality of the products? How much rack space do you give versus display space? All these little things matter,” she explained.

For retailers, this means approaching store planning as a carefully considered exercise in customer experience. Product visibility, ease of navigation, visual merchandising, and the overall look and feel of the space must work together to encourage exploration and influence buying behavior.

However, the physical environment is only one part of the equation. The human element is equally important, particularly the role played by store associates.

Mantri believes that store staff should be viewed as brand ambassadors rather than employees whose primary responsibility is billing. “The store staff cannot just be a cashier or an accountant you have hired to do the billing. They almost have to be hospitable in nature. They need to create a relationship with the customer and walk them through the buying journey.”

This relationship should extend beyond the customer's time inside the store. Associates can follow up through WhatsApp, share relevant offers, inform customers when previously unavailable products are back in stock, and even facilitate online orders when a desired product is not available at the physical location.

Such practices create continuity between online and offline channels while ensuring that retailers do not lose sales simply because of inventory limitations.

Mantri also encourages D2C brands to look beyond the immediate financial performance of their physical stores. While profitability remains important, an offline presence delivers significant intangible value by strengthening brand credibility and recognition.

**“An offline store creates a brand identity. It creates a kind of trust in the eyes of the customer that this brand has arrived. It's not an online-only brand. It exists offline,” she said.**

## **The Festive Season: India's Biggest Retail Opportunity**

In India, the festive season has traditionally been synonymous with shopping. From appliances and electronics to jewellery, fashion and lifestyle products, consumers often plan major purchases around Diwali and the months leading up to it.

As Mantri observed, many consumers deliberately postpone significant purchases until the festive period. “People wait for Diwali to buy a new fridge, a microwave and many jewellery items. They say, ‘Diwali jab aayega tab lenge.’” This consumer mindset makes October to December particularly important for the retail industry. The period encompasses pre-Diwali shopping, Diwali, pre-Christmas and Christmas purchases, followed by New Year shopping, creating a concentrated window of heightened consumption.

Recognizing this opportunity, Mantri Malls has introduced the Mantri Shopping Festival, a three-month initiative designed to make festive shopping more engaging and rewarding. The festival brings together participating brands under a larger retail celebration, with attractive discounts, offers and experiences for shoppers. Complementing this is the mall's Shopping On programme, which rewards customers based on their spending through gifts, vouchers and opportunities to win bigger prizes, including cars and bikes.

**“Our message is simple: shop and win, shop and earn with us at Mantri,” noted Mantri.**

The festival also incorporates entertainment and engagement beyond conventional retail promotions. Every year, Mantri Malls invites a prominent celebrity to launch the shopping festival, offering visitors an opportunity to interact with personalities they may otherwise only see on screen.

**For Mantri, this is an important part of the mall's role as an experience destination. “It's also a way for all our customers to meet a celebrity whom they don't get to meet on a day-to-day basis. As a mall, we kind of try to bridge that gap.”**

The festive season is also an important period for retailers to introduce new concepts, refresh existing stores and undertake renovations. Mall developments and brand launches are planned with the objective of ensuring that customers experience something new when they visit during the peak shopping months.

## **F&B: From Dining Destinations to Informal Co-working Spaces**

Another notable shift in consumer behavior is the changing role of food and beverage spaces within shopping centres. Traditionally, F&B was largely concentrated in dedicated food courts, with dining considered a complementary activity to shopping. Today, that approach is evolving rapidly.

According to Mantri, restaurants, cafés, coffee shops and bars are increasingly becoming destinations in their own right, serving purposes that extend well beyond eating and drinking.

**“An F&B outlet today is so much more than just a place where people go to grab a bite. They almost nowadays double as informal co-working spaces,” she observed.**

The appeal lies in the combination of ambience, comfort, food and flexibility. Consumers are increasingly choosing cafés and restaurants as alternative environments for meetings, creative work and casual professional interactions.

A change of setting can offer a welcome break from conventional office environments, while access to favourite beverages, food and comfortable seating makes these spaces conducive to spending extended periods of time.

Mantri pointed out that it is not unusual to find someone spending three to four hours at a coffee shop with just one coffee or a cookie. Their visit is not necessarily driven by consumption alone; it is also about finding a comfortable environment to work, unwind, or enjoy some personal space.

**This behavioral shift is influencing how malls plan their F&B offerings. “At Mantri, we understand this, and that's why F&B is no longer like earlier, when there used to be a food court, and all the food items would be only there,” she explained.**

Instead, F&B is increasingly being integrated across different floors and zones of the mall. Coffee shops, tea bars, matcha bars and other specialised concepts are strategically introduced in different areas to encourage visitors to pause, relax and spend time wherever they are.

The idea is to make food and beverage accessible throughout the mall rather than confining it to a single designated area.

## **Building the Next Chapter of Experiential Retail**

Across these three areas, a common theme emerges: retail is no longer defined solely by the transaction. Whether it is a D2C brand establishing its first physical store, a mall creating a compelling festive shopping programme or an F&B operator offering a space to work and socialise, the emphasis is increasingly on the experience surrounding consumption.

For retailers, this requires a deeper understanding of the customer journey, thoughtful investments in physical environments and a willingness to build relationships that extend beyond the point of sale.

For shopping centres, it means creating destinations that offer multiple reasons to visit, return and engage.

![Electronics Mart India Plans 25–30 New Stores in FY27, Eyes West Bengal Entry](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/2%20%281%29.jpg)

Electronics Mart India Limited (EMIL) is sharpening its expansion strategy for FY2026–27, with plans to open 25–30 new stores and enter West Bengal, beginning with Kolkata. The company is focusing on cluster-led expansion, strengthening its presence in existing markets while tapping emerging consumption centres and improving the productivity of its retail network.

The company’s expansion priorities include deepening its presence in Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Delhi-NCR, alongside building a scalable presence in West Bengal. Kolkata is emerging as a key growth market, with the company seeing potential to establish around 30 stores in the city over the next two years.

“Our expansion strategy is centred on cluster-led growth, deepening our presence in established markets while entering new geographies where we see a meaningful opportunity for organised electronics retail. We plan to open approximately 25–30 stores during FY2026–27 across existing markets and new geographies, subject to property availability, market potential and capital-allocation priorities,” said Vishal Pundir, VP, Strategy & Operations, Electronics Mart India Limited.

Beyond geographical expansion, EMIL is evaluating opportunities in growing urban centres and the expanding peripheries of existing cities, where rising residential development and improving consumer access are creating demand for organised electronics retail. However, the company is prioritising sustainable store economics over the pace of expansion.

**Location Strategy Anchored in Demand and Store Economics**

EMIL’s location-selection strategy considers multiple factors, including consumer demand, purchasing power, competitive intensity, real estate costs and supply-chain efficiencies. The company assesses household formation, population growth, consumption patterns and the presence of a growing middle-income customer base before entering a market.

Local income profiles and purchasing behaviour also influence product assortment, pricing, premium offerings and financing options. On the real estate front, visibility, accessibility, parking, frontage, floor space and delivery access are among the key considerations.

“We evaluate occupancy costs against realistic sales potential and do not want high rentals to compromise the long-term economics of a store. A location becomes more attractive when it can be supported efficiently by our warehouses, distribution network and existing store ecosystem. This helps us improve replenishment, inventory availability and logistics costs,” Pundir said.

The company also evaluates projected revenue, operating expenses, capital expenditure, inventory requirements, break-even timelines and payback periods before approving a new location. Its objective is to identify markets where consumer demand, competitive positioning and real estate economics collectively support a sustainable retail operation.

**Multi-Brand Outlets Remain Core to Retail Strategy**

EMIL continues to rely on its multi-brand outlet (MBO) format as the backbone of its retail business. At the end of FY2025–26, the company operated 215 MBOs and eight exclusive brand outlets (EBOs).

Its MBOs offer customers access to multiple leading brands across smartphones, IT products, televisions, refrigerators, air conditioners, washing machines and other consumer appliances under one roof.

Store size and format are determined by the catchment's population, purchasing power, anticipated footfall, category mix, competitive landscape and sales potential. While larger urban markets may require wider assortments and additional display space for premium products, stores in smaller cities and emerging catchments are calibrated to local demand.

“Our focus is on the productivity of every square foot. The objective is not to create the largest possible store, but to ensure that the space, assortment, inventory and operating costs are aligned with the revenue opportunity,” Pundir said.

Specialised formats and EBOs complement the MBO network by addressing specific product categories and brand experiences where there is a clear customer proposition.

**Tier II and III Markets Offer Expansion Opportunities**

The company sees significant headroom for organised electronics retail beyond major metropolitan markets. Rising aspirations, greater access to branded products, increasing digital awareness and consumer financing are supporting demand in smaller cities.

However, EMIL believes store maturity and productivity, rather than geographical classification alone, determine profitability. While established markets such as Hyderabad and other parts of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh benefit from brand familiarity, operating experience and an established supply chain, newer markets require an initial investment in building awareness and customer relationships.

“We do not assume that every Tier II or Tier III location will outperform a metropolitan market, or vice versa. We evaluate smaller-city opportunities individually, based on the addressable market, competition, customer demand and achievable sales per square foot,” Pundir said.

**Store Productivity and Premiumisation to Drive Growth**

Alongside network expansion, EMIL is banking on same-store sales growth, the maturing of newer outlets, premiumisation and operational efficiencies to strengthen its business.

Demand for premium smartphones, larger-screen televisions, advanced air conditioners, high-capacity appliances and connected-home products is creating opportunities to improve average transaction values. Stronger brand partnerships are also enabling the retailer to offer wider assortments, participate in new product launches and respond to evolving consumer preferences.

The company is also focusing on customer retention, local marketing, inventory planning, supply-chain productivity and data-led merchandising to improve existing store performance.

This strategy is reflected in its FY2026–27 first-quarter performance, with revenue from operations growing 39% year-on-year to Rs 2,419 crore, while same-store sales growth stood at 34.2%.

“A significant part of our network is relatively young. As these stores gain brand recognition, customer traffic and scale, we expect operating leverage and profitability to improve. Our growth strategy combines network expansion with higher productivity from existing stores. The objective is to build a larger business while progressively strengthening its earnings quality,” Pundir said.

**Disciplined Capital Allocation to Support Expansion**

With large-format electronics retail requiring substantial investment in store fit-outs and inventory, EMIL is maintaining a disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Management has indicated an average store fit-out capital expenditure of approximately Rs 2,500 per sq. ft. This translates into an investment of around Rs 2.5 crore for an illustrative 10,000-sq.-ft. store, excluding initial inventory requirements. Actual investments vary depending on the location and store format.

The company follows a mix of leased and owned property models, retaining flexibility in expansion while selectively considering property ownership where long-term economics justify it.

Payback periods are another important consideration. Management has indicated indicative payback periods of around 10–11 months in its established southern cluster and 16–18 months in the northern cluster. These benchmarks vary depending on market maturity and individual store performance.

“We follow a disciplined capital-allocation approach. Every store proposal is evaluated on expected revenue, gross margins, rental and employee costs, initial inventory, capital expenditure, break-even and payback. Our focus is on profitable expansion rather than expansion for its own sake,” Pundir said.

The company is also working on improving inventory turns, managing working capital and increasing throughput across its network to support better absorption of fixed costs as the business scales.

**Specialised Formats to Tap Premium Home Solutions**

Apart from its core MBO business, EMIL sees specialised retail experiences as an opportunity to strengthen customer engagement and tap premium consumption.

Its existing portfolio includes Kitchen Stories, Easy Kitchens and Audio & Beyond, which cater to specialised requirements in kitchen solutions and audio-related categories.

The company sees potential in premium kitchen appliances, home cinema, premium audio and smart-home solutions, where customers benefit from product demonstrations, consultation and guided selection. These formats can also support premiumisation by enabling consumers to evaluate integrated products based on functionality, design and suitability for their homes.

“Specialised retail experiences are an important complement to our core multi-brand business, particularly in categories where customers benefit from demonstrations, consultation and guided product selection. Our approach will remain selective and commercially disciplined. We will evaluate the size of the opportunity, customer demand, store economics, brand partnerships and the potential to scale before committing to wider expansion,” Pundir said.

As EMIL expands its geographical footprint, the company is looking to build a complementary retail ecosystem in which MBOs remain the foundation, while specialised formats deepen engagement in categories that require more immersive shopping experiences. The broader strategy is to combine wider market reach with stronger store-level productivity, premium product offerings and disciplined investment to sustain long-term growth.

![New Gurugram’s Residential Boom Drives Neighbourhood Retail Growth at Felix Plaza](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/felix.jpg)

New Gurugram’s transformation from a predominantly residential market into a growing retail and lifestyle destination is reshaping consumer shopping patterns, with neighbourhood retail centres gaining traction among families, young professionals and residents of nearby housing societies.

Felix Plaza in Sector 82A is part of this shift, bringing together more than 100 stores across 26 categories, including fashion, footwear, beauty, accessories, homeware, dining and entertainment. The destination houses brands such as H&M, Marks & Spencer, Westside, Tommy Hilfiger, Calvin Klein and Cinepolis.

According to Chirag Desai, Centre Head – Mall at Felix Plaza, the growth of organised retail in New Gurugram has followed the expansion and occupation of residential communities in the area.

“Five years ago, New Gurugram was mostly a residential story. Families moved into new housing societies, but for anything beyond daily needs they drove across the city. As those communities have filled up, retail has followed. What started as convenience retail has grown into full lifestyle destinations,” said Desai.

##### **Neighbourhood Retail Gains Ground**

The growing appeal of neighbourhood retail destinations reflects a shift in how consumers approach shopping and leisure. While established commercial hubs such as Cyber Hub and MG Road continue to attract visitors from across Gurugram, neighbourhood centres are increasingly catering to frequent, convenience-led visits.

Desai said consumers in New Gurugram tend to favour destinations that combine multiple needs, allowing them to shop, dine and socialise without travelling long distances.

“Established markets like Cyber Hub and MG Road draw people from across the city, and visits there are often planned and centred on an occasion. New Gurugram is more local, more family-led and more spontaneous. Shoppers here want variety and good value in one place,” he said.

He added that convenience extends beyond location to include parking, seating and easy movement between stores, particularly for families visiting with children and older members.

While larger malls continue to play a role in the retail ecosystem, neighbourhood destinations are becoming an option for regular weekend outings and impromptu plans. Desai noted that physical retail can differentiate itself from online and quick-commerce platforms by offering product trials, discovery and opportunities for shoppers to seek opinions before making purchases.

##### **Shopping Becomes a Leisure Activity**

Consumer behaviour at Felix Plaza varies between weekdays and weekends. Weekday visits are generally shorter and more purposeful, with customers visiting for errands, individual purchases or coffee and dinner. Weekends, in contrast, see families and groups combining shopping with dining and entertainment.

“On weekdays people come for something specific; at the weekend the visit itself becomes the outing,” Desai said.

He observed that fashion and footwear often draw consumers to the centre, while categories such as beauty, accessories and homeware encourage them to explore further. Dining and entertainment extend the duration of visits, making the overall experience an important part of the destination's retail proposition.

Families from nearby residential communities form a significant part of the weekend audience, alongside young professionals who have recently moved to New Gurugram. According to Desai, proximity encourages frequent and sometimes unplanned visits, helping build a repeat customer base.

Weekend visits also tend to involve larger groups shopping across multiple categories, which can increase spending per visit compared with weekday trips. However, the centre has not disclosed specific transaction values or repeat-visit figures.

##### **Tenant Mix Focuses on Variety and Repeat Visits**

Felix Plaza's retail strategy centres on bringing together established brands and emerging labels across different price points and categories. The aim is to cater to consumers with varied preferences while encouraging them to spend more time at the destination.

“Our aim is for different tastes and budgets to share one afternoon. We balance fashion and footwear, which bring people in, with beauty, accessories, homeware, dining and entertainment, which turn a quick errand into a full outing,” Desai said.

He added that maintaining a sustainable neighbourhood retail destination requires regular attention to the tenant mix and the overall customer experience. While proximity can attract initial visits, retaining customers depends on fresh offerings, effective brand engagement and an environment that encourages repeat visits.

The centre also focuses on practical amenities, including valet services, pram services and convenient movement between stores. These features are intended to improve accessibility for families and support longer visits.

For retailers, sustained footfall must translate into sales for the destination to remain commercially viable. Desai said balancing the tenant mix with the customer experience is important for tenant retention and occupancy.

##### **Expansion and Community-Led Experiences**

Felix Plaza plans to continue developing its tenant mix by adding brands that reflect New Gurugram's changing consumer profile, including emerging labels alongside established retailers. The centre also intends to strengthen its dining and leisure offerings.

Community-led initiatives, including festive celebrations, family-oriented weekends and brand activations, are expected to form part of its strategy to encourage repeat visits and position the centre as a social destination for nearby residents.

Looking ahead, Desai is optimistic about the centre's growth prospects over the next 12–24 months, supported by the continued development and occupation of housing societies in New Gurugram.

“We are optimistic. New Gurugram’s population keeps growing as more housing societies are completed and occupied, which steadily widens our catchment. These residents want a weekend destination close enough for an impromptu plan, with enough to do that nobody watches the clock. That demand will be the main driver of our growth,” he said.

As residential development continues to reshape New Gurugram, neighbourhood retail destinations such as Felix Plaza are positioning themselves around convenience, category diversity and experience-led shopping. Their long-term performance, however, will depend on converting local catchment demand into consistent store sales, repeat visits and sustainable tenant performance.

![From Festive Splurges to Everyday Luxury: Changing Consumer Trends in India’s Premium Footwear Market](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Sahil.jpg)

India’s premium footwear market is witnessing a shift in consumer behaviour, with demand gradually expanding beyond weddings and festive occasions to everyday luxury purchases. While festivals and weddings continue to drive seasonal sales, consumers are increasingly investing in premium footwear as part of their regular wardrobes.

Sahil Malik, CEO of Da Milano and Rosso Brunello, has observed this shift firsthand, noting that footwear is increasingly becoming an integral part of consumers’ everyday style choices rather than remaining limited to special occasions.

“Traditionally, in our country, sales have always been higher during the festive period. Weddings and festivals propel demand, and luxury shopping goes up during these occasions. Footwear is an important part of the overall ensemble, with consumers looking to complement their outfits,” Malik said.

However, he believes the market is undergoing a broader transformation, driven by consumers’ growing interest in quality products, established brands and everyday style.

“What I have witnessed over the last few years is that people are now looking to buy footwear on a regular basis as well. I feel the shift is towards everyday luxury rather than just the festive period. Consumers want to look good and invest in great products and brands. Everyday luxury is coming in a big way,” he added.

##### **Everyday Luxury Reshapes Premium Footwear Demand**

The growing preference for everyday luxury signals an opportunity for premium footwear brands to expand their consumer base beyond occasion-led shopping. Instead of purchasing premium footwear only for weddings, festivals or formal events, consumers are increasingly considering it for work, social outings and daily wear.

This shift could also influence how brands approach product design, pricing and retail strategies. Versatility, comfort and durability, alongside aesthetics and brand value, are likely to become important considerations for consumers seeking to incorporate premium footwear into their everyday lives.

For brands such as Da Milano and Rosso Brunello, the trend presents an opportunity to build more frequent consumer engagement and encourage repeat purchases beyond peak festive seasons.

As consumers increasingly view premium footwear as an everyday style investment, the category’s growth could become less dependent on seasonal demand and more closely linked to changing lifestyle aspirations.

The emerging trend points to a wider evolution in India’s premium retail market, where luxury is increasingly being incorporated into everyday consumption rather than being reserved exclusively for special occasions.
